abstracts.value: Accurate characterization of quantum dynamics is essential for the calibration and control of quantum devices. Unknown state preparation and measurement (SPAM) errors, however, introduce gauge ambiguities that limit what can be learned. A central question is therefore which properties are learnable despite SPAM errors, and whether physical structure in the dynamics can restrict these ambiguities and expand the set of learnable properties. In this work, we address both questions within a unified framework for quantum channels and continuous-time evolution. First, for general quantum channels and Lindbladian dynamics, we use the cycle structure of a generalized pattern-transfer graph to fully characterize all learnable parameter combinations and show achievability by constructing explicit SPAM-robust learning protocols, establishing a baseline where continuous gauge freedom prevents many individual parameters from being identified. Second, we show that coherent structure drastically restricts this gauge ambiguity, reducing continuous gauge freedom to discrete or even trivial choices. This restriction manifests across both discrete- and continuous-time settings, including purely Hamiltonian evolution, noisy quantum channels close to a target unitary, and Lindbladian dynamics close to a target Hamiltonian. In particular, when the dynamics preserves or remains close to a coherent Hamiltonian form, all coherent coefficients and broad classes of dissipative error parameters become individually learnable. These results establish a systematic route to exploiting physical structure for SPAM-robust characterization, providing a foundation for the reliable calibration and control of quantum devices.

titles.title: SPAM-robust learnability of quantum dynamics

abstracts.value: We discuss a possible early Universe scenario, where radiation era is interrupted by the epoch of domination of domain walls eventually annihilating into particles. During this period the Universe undergoes accelerated expansion, while the comoving correlation length of the domain wall network remains constant. The spectral shape of gravitational waves predicted in this scenario is markedly different compared to the case of domain walls remaining sub-dominant all the way till annihilation. abstracts.value: Tip of the red giant branch (TRGB)-based determinations of the Hubble constant ($H_0$), the current expansion rate of the Universe, depend on choices made in selecting and analyzing stellar photometry and in assembling the sample of calibrator galaxies hosting Type Ia supernovae (SNe Ia). The CosmoVerse Data Challenge invites participants to analyze public photometric catalogs within a shared distance-ladder framework, opening each step of the measurement to the community and testing how these choices propagate into $H_0$. Participants independently selected photometric catalogs, galaxies, and TRGB measurement settings, while using a common SN Ia compilation and fitting procedure to convert distances into $H_0$. Supported by public notebooks and a training school, the challenge received 26 submissions from 22 participants. All submissions used the same analysis notebook, many participants were trainees at the school, and the true galaxy distances are unknown; the results therefore characterize the sensitivity of the submissions to analysis and sample-selection choices and are not a combined determination of $H_0$ or an estimate of the systematic uncertainty in published TRGB measurements. The inferred $H_0$ values have a median of $77.10\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}\,Mpc^{-1}}$ and a standard deviation of $7.38\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}\,Mpc^{-1}}$$(5.11\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}\,Mpc^{-1}}$ for the scaled median absolute deviation), $\sim 3.4$$(\sim 2.4)$ times the typical quoted uncertainty of a submission. abstracts.value: Noise typically destroys quantum coherence and washes out transport phenomena that rely on interference. Chiral quantum walks are a case in point: a particle hopping on a lattice threaded by a magnetic flux can spread asymmetrically due to interference between paths, an asymmetry that noise is expected to erase. Remarkably, we find that the most ubiquitous noise -- random fluctuations of on-site energies (dephasing) -- instead renders this asymmetry topologically robust. The density profile develops a skewness that grows in time while its center stays fixed, and in a finite chain the late-time relaxation modes pile up at one edge: a skin effect lacking the drift of conventional non-Hermitian skin effects. With multiple sites per unit cell, the dephasing strength alone can cause a topological phase transition, reversing the asymmetry. On a flux ladder with noisy rung hopping, the noise causes a drift of rung coherences, a quantum ratchet with no classical counterpart. Underlying these effects, the noise-averaged dynamics is an interacting (generically non-integrable) Lindbladian that remains analytically tractable. The modes governing late-time relaxation are bound states of the noise-induced interaction and form a band with a point gap, absent both without noise and under postselection, whose winding number fixes the direction of the asymmetry. These effects are within reach of several experimental platforms, including synthetic lattices, superconducting qubits, and optical lattices.

abstracts.value: Designing a superconducting quantum processor rests on predicting the low-lying spectrum of its coupled circuit. The Hilbert-space dimension of the circuit's lumped-element model grows exponentially with the number of circuit nodes. We present a tensor-network method that chooses no subsystems and whose memory and run time per solve are set by the number of modes and two truncations, the Fock cutoff of each normal mode and the bond dimension of a matrix product state (MPS), not by the Hilbert-space dimension. From the capacitance matrix, the inverse-inductance matrix and the junction list alone, the linear circuit is diagonalized into normal modes. Each junction cosine is then a sum of two products of single-mode operators, so the complete lumped-element Hamiltonian is a matrix product operator (MPO) of small bond dimension with one site per mode, solved by the density matrix renormalization group (DMRG). The normal modes make the method generic, and the tensor network makes it affordable. For two fluxonia joined by a tunable coupler, the method agrees with exact diagonalization of the same truncated space to within 1 MHz. Our circuit of three fluxonia joined by two couplers has 11 normal modes and a truncated space of $10^9$ states, out of reach of exact diagonalization in dense or sparse storage. At a bond dimension of 32, its lowest eight levels are converged to within 1 MHz in both truncations, and each state is stored in a small fraction of the numbers a dense vector needs. Virtual HNLs modify electroweak gauge-boson propagation and lepton couplings through loops with two dipole interactions. We calculate the resulting finite matching corrections and their effects on $Z$-pole observables. For real, flavour-aligned couplings, the local response is specified by four combinations of coupling shifts. Independent local ultraviolet interactions can reproduce all four, making the dipole interpretation dependent on assumptions about those interactions. With improved Standard Model predictions, FCC-ee can probe equal, same-sign hypercharge and weak dipole coefficients as small as $0.14\,\mathrm{TeV}^{-2}$ at an HNL mass of 1 TeV. This projection assumes dipole dominance, with independent ultraviolet coefficients set to zero at twice the HNL mass. We quantify how additional ultraviolet contributions can weaken or strengthen the sensitivity. At 1 TeV, the projected reach is competitive with HL-LHC same-sign dilepton searches for Majorana HNLs, while larger masses allow smaller dipole coefficients to be probed within the effective theory's domain of validity. Radiative Higgs decays offer a modest further improvement. The FeynRules, FeynArts and UFO models used in this analysis are publicly available at \href{https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23667622}{doi:10.5281/zenodo.23667622}.

titles.title: Indirect probes of heavy neutral leptons through the dipole portal at FCC-ee

abstracts.value: Instantaneous quantum polynomial-time (IQP) Born machines are attractive quantum generative models, as certain IQP circuit families are conjectured to be hard to sample, yet they can be trained classically. Previously proposed conditional IQP Born machines make the parameters of the diagonal layer condition dependent. We introduce conditional IQP Born machines, in which the condition is encoded in the input state and a single IQP unitary is shared across conditions. Efficient sampling and amplitude-ratio evaluation for the reference state entering the diagonal layer suffice to obtain unbiased classical estimates of a conditional maximum mean discrepancy objective and its gradients. We show that input conditioning can represent conditional families that no diagonally conditioned IQP model with the same number of qubits can reproduce. For the sixteen-qubit Curie-Weiss spin model, a single conditional model captures the magnetization transition at held-out temperatures. Its mean total variation distance is six times lower than that of diagonal conditioning under the same protocol and comparable to that of classical generative models with up to seven times as many parameters. We also train conditional models classically with up to 2048 qubits, which reproduce the mean squared magnetization of the target away from the crossover. These results extend classically trained IQP Born machines to conditional generation.

titles.title: Classical training of conditional instantaneous quantum polynomial-time Born machines

abstracts.value: The Euclid spectroscopic surveys will substantially increase the number of observed emission-line galaxies. We assess the ability of the Euclid Wide Survey (EWS) and Euclid Deep Survey (EDS), at the final DR3 depth, to recover the star-forming main sequence (MS), dust-mass relation (DMR), and mass-metallicity relation (MZR) from emission-line measurements. We use MAMBO (mocks with abundance matching in Bologna) spectroscopic simulations processed with the official Euclid pipelines. The MS is traced over $0\leq z\leq 4$ using Pa$β$, H$α$, and [OII] as SFR tracers. The shallow EWS flux limit biases the MS towards higher normalisation and a flatter slope by selecting the brightest, most strongly star-forming galaxies. The deeper EDS enables almost complete sampling with Pa$β$ and H$α$ at log$_{10}(M_*/M_\odot)\geq10.3$ over $0\leq z\leq 1.88$, with mild biases at both redshift limits. The [OII]-based MS is increasingly biased towards higher SFRs at the highest redshifts. The DMR is traced through the Balmer decrement over $1.45\leq z\leq 1.88$ and $0.9\leq z\leq 1.88$ in the EWS and EDS, respectively. The derived colour excess agree well with the input values, although detecting the faint H$β$ line restricts the sample to less obscured galaxies at fixed $M_*$, particularly in the EWS; the DMR is better sampled in the EDS. Finally, a golden sample detected in multiple optical rest-frame emission lines at $1.49\leq z\leq 1.88$ recovers gas-phase metallicities with typical accuracy of 0.1 dex at log$_{10}(M_*/M_\odot)\geq10$, while lower-mass galaxies show biases up to 0.15 dex. Relative to H-band limited sample, this sample preferentially traces the upper MS and lower MZR. Despite the simplified simulations lacking effects such as mutual spectral contamination and detector persistence, these forecasts provide a benchmark for future Euclid spectroscopic analyses.

titles.title: Euclid. Predicting scaling relations for emission-line galaxies using simulated data

abstracts.value: In the high energy Regge asymptotics of QCD, the rapid overpopulation of gluons leads to gluon saturation, characterized by nonperturbative semi-classical lumpy configurations of size $1/Q_S$, where $Q_S\gg Λ_{\rm QCD}$ is a dynamical semi-hard saturation scale. We discuss here a generalization of the Color Glass Condensate (CGC) framework describing this phenomenon that is obtained by carefully treating the breaking of global symmetries by the condensate. In particular, we show that the breaking of a global subgroup of color results in a Goldstone effective field theory (EFT) whose dynamics is characterized by a Goldstone decay constant $f_G = \sqrt{N} Q_S$, where $N=O(1/α_S)$ is the phase space occupancy of the condensate, which is large for $α_S(Q_S)\ll 1$. Further, the coupling of these colored Goldstones to collinear gluon modes leads to a depletion of the condensate, thereby modifying the static shockwave scattering framework of the CGC on timescales controlled by $f_G$. The CGC EFT on these longer time scales is a novel color superfluid. Low frequency modes with $ω\leq α_S Q_S$ in an external probe of the CGC are sensitive to superfluid dynamics, with interesting physical consequences for deeply inelastic scattering and ultrarelativistic nuclear collisions.

titles.title: Goldstone theory of gluon saturation in high energy QCD: From color glass to color superfluid condensate

abstracts.value: Pure states of four and seven qubits cannot be maximally entangled across every balanced bipartition; we determine how entangled they can be on average. For four qubits we prove the conjecture of Higuchi and Sudbery: the mean von Neumann entropy of the three $2|2$ cuts is at most $1+\tfrac12\log_2 3$ bits, with equality exactly on the local-unitary orbits of their state $M_4$ and its complex conjugate. For seven qubits the mean purity of the 35 balanced $3|4$ cuts is at least $121/917$ and their mean entropy is at most $2.965356029\ldots$ bits, each with a unique optimiser up to local unitaries and qubit permutations. The two optimisers are distinct members of one icosahedral family, so minimum purity and maximum entropy select different states. The proofs bound moments of the marginal spectra by positive identities on several copies of the state, some of them spin flipped, and bound the entropy by a polynomial in those moments. The four-qubit maximum has an analytic proof; the seven-qubit proofs, and some of the four-qubit refinements below, are computer-assisted, with exact arithmetic and rigorous error bounds. We also prove the Gour--Wallach conjecture for Rényi entropies of all orders, with the maximiser changing from $M_4$ to cluster states at $q_*\approx1.588$, and obtain sharp Tsallis bounds, mixed-state bounds and quantitative stability.

titles.title: The most entangled states of four and seven qubits

abstracts.value: We present measurements of the mass of the Milky Way using distant halo stars selected from the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI) Data Release 2 (DR2). We apply four dynamical modeling methods to 10,036 RR Lyrae (RRL) and blue horizontal branch (BHB) stars with 6D phase space coordinates that span from $\sim$10 to 95 kpc from the Galactic center, the largest samples of their kind. All methods are applied to mock surveys based on cosmological simulations that include generating individual tracer stars, convolving their phase-space coordinates with DESI and Gaia DR3-like uncertainties, and tailored models of the survey selection functions. By comparing the performance on these mocks, we quantify how systematic biases from both methodology assumptions and galaxy disequilibrium impact each estimate. The mock-based systematics, which differ by method and tracer, are used to correct the individual estimates and to derive joint estimates using a rigorous formalism that accounts for per-method biases and residual correlations between methods. We obtain a joint estimate of the mass within 80 kpc to be $M(r < 80 \mathrm{\,kpc}) = 6.36^{+0.53}_{-0.48} \times 10^{11}$ M$_\odot$ and a virial mass estimate of $M_\mathrm{200c} = 1.19^{+0.14}_{-0.12} \times 10^{12}$ M$_\odot$, with similar results when combining only RRL-based or BHB-based measurements. These results provide a roadmap for future DESI efforts, as well as those in other spectroscopic surveys, to reliably constrain the mass of our Galaxy.

titles.title: DESI DR2 Results III: The Mass of the Milky Way

abstracts.value: The Lindblad master equation is the standard framework for describing dissipative dynamics of the open quantum system context. Its conventional derivation, however, relies on the rotating-wave approximation (RWA), which neglects the counter rotating terms in the system-reservoir interaction. Here, we derive a generalized Lindblad master equation beyond the RWA within the density operator formalism, retaining the full systemreservoir coupling. We consider two prototypical open quantum systems, a two-level atom and a single-mode quantized field, each interacting with thermal or squeezed reservoirs described by the Wigner-Weisskopf theory. The resulting master equations are applied to the evolution of representative physical observables and compared with the conventional RWA based formulation. We show that counter-rotating terms produce significant modifications to the dissipative dynamics and therefore cannot, in general, be neglected. For a thermal reservoir, increasing the mean thermal photon number, nth, enhances the decay of hσ^yi beyond the RWA but suppresses it within the RWA. Likewise, the evolution of hσ^zi exhibits opposite damping behavior with increasing Γt and squeezing parameter r. These findings demonstrate the importance of including counter rotating terms for an accurate description of open quantum systems.

titles.title: Quantum theory of damping: A new approach to temporal evolution of density operator without the rotating wave approximation

abstracts.value: We present a theoretically constrained phenomenological reconstruction of the unpolarized, chiral-even, leading-twist proton generalized parton distributions $H^q$ and $E^q$. At zero skewness, valence-quark distributions are combined with flavor-dependent exponential profiles calibrated simultaneously against phenomenological representations of the proton and neutron electromagnetic form factors. The construction imposes exact valence and anomalous-magnetic-moment normalizations, the low-scale condition $B^{u+d}(0)=0$, the required endpoint behavior, and the complete Gaussian impact-parameter positivity bound. The resulting parametrization provides a reasonable description of the electromagnetic form factors and their slopes while revealing the tension between strict GPD consistency and a precision reproduction of all low-$Q^2$ observables within the adopted ansatz. We extend the distributions to nonzero skewness using normalized double distributions and introduce an independent $D$-term to complete the relevant Mellin polynomials. We examine electromagnetic and energy--momentum-tensor form factors, impact-parameter distributions, positivity, polynomiality, and illustrative mechanical properties. The analysis distinguishes information constrained by electromagnetic data from additional assumptions governing skewness and the mechanical sector, thereby providing a transparent elastic baseline for future studies of nucleon-to-resonance transition GPDs.

titles.title: Proton generalized parton distributions from electromagnetic form factors: A theoretically constrained phenomenological reconstruction

abstracts.value: Most quantum-computer security work targets physical-layer attacks on qubits, while two surfaces remain inadequately defended: the quantum-error-correction (QEC) syndrome-and-decoder pipeline, and the classical control and software stack that runs it. Tampering on these surfaces can corrupt a computation while the physical error rate appears normal, and can stay within a single-circuit integrity tolerance. We present Trinetra.Q, a detection layer of cooperating detectors, each monitoring a statistical or behavioral property of quantum-domain data against an envelope calibrated from honest operation, and raising an indication only on a statistically significant deviation. The detectors cover (A) QEC integrity over per-stabilizer firing rates, syndrome defect-count, and repeated-syndrome rate; (B) decoder confidence over the margin between minimum-weight error explanations in distinct logical classes; (C) behavioral output divergence, flagging crosstalk-class and novel attacks by their effect on a victim's output relative to a matched control; (D) control-stack tampering via known-answer canary circuits, built to be indistinguishable to a resident implant, with a cross-job consistency statistic; and (E) compilation/execution integrity. Each gates on significance, so honest operation raises no alarm. We evaluate in faithful simulation and on three production IBM Heron processors, and bound the physical attack surface with a systematic negative map: most physical-layer attacks return statistically null, the exception an implemented, measured within-job feed-forward covert-channel primitive. Every detector is also evaluated against an adaptive attacker with full knowledge of it. To our knowledge this is the first unified statistical-and-behavioral detection layer for the QEC layer and classical control stack of a quantum computing system, demonstrated on production hardware.

titles.title: Trinetra.Q: Statistical and Behavioral Detection of Attacks on the Quantum-Error-Correction Layer and Classical Control Stack of Quantum Computing Systems

abstracts.value: Establishing multipartite entanglement across lossy optical networks remains a central challenge for distributed quantum information processing. Here, we consider a non-Gaussian continuous-variable entanglement-swapping protocol combining a symmetric discrete Fourier transform (DFT) interferometer with photon-number-resolving detection. In the ideal limit, single-photon heralding generates a $W_N$-class state across remote modes, with Fourier symmetry rendering all single-click outcomes equivalent up to local phase corrections. We find that conditional pairwise entanglement can exceed that of conventional Gaussian homodyne swapping in weak-to-moderate squeezing and lossy regimes, remaining nonzero beyond the channel-loss thresholds at which Gaussian pairwise entanglement vanishes. These results demonstrate that combining non-Gaussian measurements with symmetric interferometric mixing can improve both the resilience and operational efficiency of multipartite entanglement distribution in lossy quantum networks.

titles.title: Multipartite entanglement swapping with homodyne and single photon detection

abstracts.value: Integrated photonics provides a promising route towards the development of large-scale, stable and low-loss quantum hardware. Existing implementations of universal quantum photonic chips generally rely on architectures consisting of localised interactions between the modes that can be programmed with known algorithms to implement specific operations. Recent advances have shown that interferometers based on 3D continuously coupled waveguide arrays may allow to significantly scale up the number of modes with reduced overhead. However, for this class of devices, optimal strategies to set the controllable parameters and obtain the desired transformation have not been demonstrated generally. In this work, we report the use of a machine learning algorithm driven by quantum data to program the operation of a reconfigurable three-dimensional continuously coupled photonic device comprising 128 modes. We show experimentally the capability of reaching a target unitary matrix, among those achievable by the device, through a limited number of one- and two-photon measurements. Our results demonstrate that this approach results to be effective in the presence of noise and with a limited amount of resources, also allowing to partially compensate imperfections in the experimental setup. This method can thus represent a viable route towards programming large scale integrated photonic devices, unlocking the possibility of controlling photonic systems for which an analytical decomposition is not trivial.

titles.title: Efficient training of a 128-modes 3D continuously coupled photonic chip via limited quantum resources

abstracts.value: The remnants of binary black-hole (BBH) mergers are accurately described by numerical relativity, but the physical principle governing the selection of the final states remains unclear. A recently proposed maximum-entropy conjecture suggests that a BBH merger produces the Kerr BH that maximizes the Bekenstein-Hawking entropy, subject to the post-Newtonian formalism or balance laws for energy and angular momentum. In this work, we test this conjecture with the event GW250114, inferring the progenitor and remnant properties from the observed pre-merge and post-merge signals, separately. We construct the surrogate Kerr entropy associated with candidate remnant states along the inferred energy-angular-momentum trajectory. We then compare the maximum-entropy state with the independently inferred mass and dimensionless spin of the final BH. We find that the conjecture predicts a remnant mass of $M_f=70.0^{+0.35}_{-0.21}\,M_\odot$ and spin of $χ_f=0.70^{+0.00}_{-0.01}$, compared with the ringdown estimates $M_f={72.3}^{+3.6}_{-3.7}\,M_\odot$ and $χ_f=0.74^{+0.05}_{-0.07}$. The entropy deviation is consistent with zero within the $68\%$ credible interval for our fiducial analysis, and variations in the pre-merger truncation time and quasi-normal modes (QNM) content reveal no compelling discrepancy with the conjecture.

titles.title: Observational Test of the Maximum-Entropy Conjecture for Black-Hole Mergers with GW250114

abstracts.value: Defining entropy of a quantum channel has become a challenge with potential candidates recently reported in literature. In this Article, it is taken under consideration the entropy of a quantum channel defined as the quantum entropy of its associated Choi state. The consequences presented here of such approach is two-fold. First, the limitations on the information-processing of quantum channels are assessed, leading to the \emph{higher-order quantum information inequalities}. Those are then considered as useful witnesses of non-Markovian effects beyond a given number of quantum side-channels in a quantum process. Importantly, the presentation is given with the application of the methods for the study of examples. Second, such approach provides a characterization on the condition for the recovery of quantum channel preparations under non-Markovian noise. Such result is a straightforward extension of standard error-correction conditions which gives further meaning to the higher-order information measures defined here.

titles.title: Higher-order quantum information inequalities and error-correction of non-Markovian noise

abstracts.value: The Euclid mission will revolutionize our understanding of the visible Universe by collecting images and spectra of millions of galaxies across cosmic time and environments. Here, we forecast the number counts of galaxies emitting [OII], H{̱e̱ṯa̱}̱, [OIII], Hα and Pa{̱e̱ṯa̱}̱ lines in the Euclid Wide Survey (EWS) and Deep Survey (EDS). We compare predictions from different models, including semi-analytic models and empirical scaling relations. We then simulate spectra for galaxies in the MAMBO lightcone using FastSpec, designed to rapidly generate one-dimensional spectra as observed by Euclid. We process these simulated spectra with the official Euclid spectroscopic pipeline to recover redshifts and line fluxes and derive expected counts. Predictions for Hα+[NII] emitters are broadly consistent across mocks and with existing observations. In the EWS, relative RMS scatter among mock predictions for integrated counts is approximately 19% for Hα+[NII], 44% for [OII] and 41% for [OIII], reflecting greater model dependence for oxygen-line forecasts. After accounting for flux losses and redshift misidentification, corrected flux measurements recover most intrinsic line counts, especially in the EDS. From the MAMBO-based FastSpec simulations, we predict that Euclid will detect about 42 million Hα emitters in the EWS and 1.7 million in the EDS. The same simulations predict approximately 0.5 and 0.8 million [OII] and [OIII] emitters, respectively, in the EDS, and about 1.3 and 7.5 million in the EWS. These non-Hα forecasts remain subject to substantial model-dependent uncertainties, as shown by scatter among the different mocks. These samples will be instrumental in pushing large-scale structure and baryon acoustic oscillation studies beyond redshift z~2, extending Euclid cosmological and galaxy evolution studies beyond what is achievable with Hα alone.

titles.title: Euclid: Forecasting the number counts of bright line emitters in the Euclid Wide Survey and Euclid Deep fields

abstracts.value: We study a mixed block encoding of quantum-chemistry Hamiltonians for quantum phase estimation (QPE) on fault-tolerant quantum computers. Following a Cholesky decomposition of the electron repulsion integral tensor, we assign each Cholesky tensor to either a double-factorization (DF) branch or a sparse-single-factorization (SPSF) branch. This freedom permits a trade-off between reducing the block-encoding normalization factor $λ$ with DF and reducing the coefficient data loaded through quantum read-only memory (QROM) with SPSF. Resource estimates across molecular benchmarks show, however, that the mixed circuit does not generally reduce the Toffoli count relative to the less expensive pure circuit. The main obstacles are the overhead of loading substantial data through separate branch-specific QROMs and the limited benefit of mixing when the pure DF and SPSF circuits have dissimilar costs. Modest savings occur only in restricted parameter regimes, most clearly when logical-qubit requirements are included in the cost metric. These results identify the circuit-level conditions that a useful mixed block encoding must satisfy.

titles.title: Quantum resource trade-offs of mixed sparse single and double factorization for qubitization-based phase estimation

abstracts.value: The rate at which quantum fluctuations of observables can change provides a useful characterization of the dynamical behavior of quantum systems. For closed quantum systems undergoing unitary evolution, previous work has established a general upper bound on the growth rate of the uncertainty of an observable in terms of the standard deviation of its dynamical velocity. This result is closely related to quantum acceleration limits and provides a compact constraint on fluctuation growth. In this work, we will briefly review the closed system results and extend this perspective to open quantum systems, where the state evolves nonunitarily as a consequence of interactions with an environment. The central result is an upper bound on the rate of growth of the uncertainty of an observable that remains valid for general density-matrix dynamics. We develop two complementary derivations. The first introduces a Hermitian pseudo-Hamiltonian describing the local unitary evolution of the eigenvectors of the density matrix. The second, and more general, derivation proceeds directly from the density-matrix derivative and therefore does not require knowledge of the generator of the dynamics. Both approaches lead to the same fluctuation-growth bound. An important practical advantage is that the bound can be evaluated from the observable, the state, and its time derivative without requiring reconstruction of the complete dynamical generator.

titles.title: A Study of Fluctuation Growths of Observables in Open Quantum Systems

abstracts.value: Quantum information science (QIS) offers a new set of conceptual and computational tools ideally suited to exploring the many-body, out-of-equilibrium, and real-time properties of strongly interacting quantum systems. These themes find a natural counterpart in high energy nuclear physics, whose central goal is to describe the properties of Quantum Chromodynamics (QCD), the theory of the strong interaction, under extreme conditions. Relevant examples range from the formation and internal structure of hadrons, to the collective and thermalization dynamics of strongly interacting QCD matter, and the properties of complex many-body scattering processes. Although tremendous progress has been made over the past decades in our understanding of QCD in the nuclear physics context, through perturbative methods, lattice QCD, and effective theory descriptions, phenomena that are intrinsically connected to real-time dynamics, highly entangled many-body evolution, or finite density regimes remain only partially accessible with existing approaches. In this article, we argue that QIS can help realize a new paradigm for addressing these open questions. With the aim of making the discussion accessible to both high energy nuclear physics and QIS audiences, we provide an overview of selected open problems in high energy nuclear physics, with emphasis on aspects motivated by collider phenomenology, and discuss how they can be approached using QIS tools. This connection is illustrated through representative examples drawn from the recent literature, making the case that QIS can become a driving force for discovery in nuclear physics in the coming years.

titles.title: Quantum computing for high energy nuclear physics

abstracts.value: Since primordial black holes (PBH) are always non-relativistic, their cosmological energy fraction grows relative to that of radiation. Thus, for even a tiny initial PBH abundance, the universe generically enters an epoch of early matter domination, which ends when the PBH evaporate to restore the hot big bang. We consider the possibility that a PBH dominated era yields a population of boosted axion-like particles (ALPs) produced from Hawking evaporation. Eventually these ``Hawking axions" become non-relativistic and decay to photons, which can affect various cosmological and astrophysical observables. Here we place new constraints on these particles through their impact on big bang nucleosynthesis, cosmic microwave background, large-scale structure, and X-ray observables. Furthermore, if Hawking axions remain relativistic through recombination, then depending on the progenitor PBH mass, they contribute $ΔN_{\rm eff}\simeq0.05$-$0.11$, which may be observable with future CMB probes.

titles.title: The Cosmology of Hawking Axions

abstracts.value: Persistent radio sources (PRSs) associated with repeating fast radio bursts probe the immediate magneto-ionic environment of their engine and thereby constrain the nature and evolutionary stage of the progenitor. The persistent radio source of FRB20201124A is the most extreme in the current sample, with a spectrum that remains flat or inverted up to 22 GHz. We aim to constrain the centimetre-to-millimetre spectral energy distribution of this source and to test whether its properties are consistent with a young, rotation-powered magnetar wind nebula. We analysed archival ALMA Band 3 observations at $\sim100$ GHz and combined them with existing VLA measurements at 6, 15 and 22 GHz. The resulting spectrum was fitted with the Granot--Sari broken power law in the slow-cooling regime using Bayesian nested sampling. The two-parameter model yields a peak frequency $ν_m = 63^{+100}_{-33}$ GHz and a peak flux $F_m = 28\pm9$$μ$Jy. This solution is consistent with theoretical expectations for a young magnetar wind nebula, which predict a peak frequency in the same range and a self-absorption frequency below $\sim0.5$ GHz. With its inverted spectrum extending to tens of gigahertz and the highest peak frequency among known PRSs, the source associated with FRB20201124A is the most extreme in the current sample. Its properties match those expected for a rotation-powered magnetar wind nebula, making it a strong candidate for the youngest ($t\lesssim20$ yr) magnetar associated with a repeating FRB to date.

titles.title: A high-frequency turnover in the persistent radio source of FRB20201124A

abstracts.value: The electron--phonon (e-ph) interaction underlies conventional superconductivity and plays a central role in transport and other many-body phenomena in solids. Here, we derive a symmetry selection rule for e-ph scattering in two-dimensional crystals possessing a horizontal mirror plane, $σ_h$. For electronic states of mirror parity $s_n(\mathbf{k})$ and $s_m(\mathbf{k}+\mathbf{q})$, and a phonon mode of parity $χ_ν(\mathbf{q})$, we show that the e-ph matrix element $g_{mn,ν}(\mathbf{k},\mathbf{q})$ vanishes identically unless $s_n(\mathbf{k})\,χ_ν(\mathbf{q})\, s_m(\mathbf{k}+\mathbf{q})=+1$. The rule follows from the covariance of the phonon-induced deformation potential under $σ_h$, constitutes the $C_s$ case of the general group-theoretical selection rule for matrix elements, and partitions the e-ph interaction throughout the Brillouin zone into symmetry-allowed and symmetry-forbidden scattering channels. Consequently, mirror-even phonons couple electronic states of the same mirror parity, either even--even or odd--odd, whereas mirror-odd phonons couple only states of opposite mirror parity, for both intra- and interband processes. We illustrate the selection rule through first-principles calculations for the two-dimensional superconductor $\mathrm{Sc_2BCH_4}$, where mirror parity is well defined throughout the entire Brillouin zone and symmetry-forbidden matrix elements vanish up to numerical precision. We then extend the analysis to bulk $\mathrm{MgB_2}$, where the rule applies exactly only on mirror-invariant planes of the three-dimensional Brillouin zone. Moving away from these planes removes the exact mirror constraint and activates scattering channels that are symmetry forbidden when the mirror eigenvalues are well defined. Our results establish horizontal mirror symmetry as an exact and practical filter of e-ph scattering processes.

titles.title: Exact Mirror-Parity Selection Rule for Electron-Phonon Coupling in Two-Dimensional Crystals

abstracts.value: Because of the fermion doubling problem, it has been a longstanding challenge to describe a lattice algorithm for studying four-dimensional gauge theories coupled to chiral fermions. Recently, an algorithm to do so has been described by Craig, extending partial results in the previous literature. Here we describe a variant of this algorithm, based on interpolating a lattice gauge field over the continuum (as in Craig's work) and coupling the interpolated gauge field to continuum chiral fermions. The same variant was also proposed recently by Hsu. In any dimension and for any anomaly-free representation, this approach can be implemented on a computer in principle, but not in practice by Monte Carlo methods because the chiral fermion path integral is not positive.

titles.title: A Note On Lattice Definition of Gauge Theories With Chiral Fermions

As a first step the Remler formalism is tested in <math><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>p</mi></mrow></math> collisions and then applied to <math><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>A</mi></mrow></math> collisions in order to extract the nuclear absorption cross section of charmonium, which is then utilized in heavy-ion collisions. We find that the Remler formalism successfully describes charmonium production in heavy-ion collisions at SPS energies when an in-medium heavy quark potential is implemented, in which <math><mrow><mi>J</mi><mo>/</mo><mi>ψ</mi></mrow></math> dissociates near <math><msub><mi>T</mi><mi>c</mi></msub></math>. abstracts.value: In our previous article CMP 407 (2026) 131, we explored the rich algebraic structures arising from a specific quantum many-body Hamiltonian quartic in the bosonic creation-annihilation operators. This Hamiltonian originated from the works of Gérard and Grellier on classical turbulent energy transfer in a Lax-integrable setting, and its quantum version respects hierarchies of polynomial conservation laws all of which possess purely integer spectra, as does the Hamiltonian itself. The latter feature, known from numerical studies, has previously remained unproved. Here, we present an elementary solution of the quantum Gérard-Grellier Hamiltonian. The eigenstates are labelled by partitions and the corresponding eigenvalues admit simple explicit expressions in terms of the principal hook lengths. The key ingredient in this construction is a specific basis we introduce, inspired by the classical multisoliton coherent states, in which the Hamiltonian is upper-triangular. The expressions for the eigenvalues then immediately follow, while the full eigenbasis can be recovered via a Gram-Schmidt procedure.

abstracts.value: We construct an exact map between continuum fermion fields and lattice fields in 1+1 dimensions. This map rewrites a continuum Hamiltonian as a lattice Hamiltonian with nearest-neighbor couplings and an infinite-dimensional local Hilbert space. The resulting lattice model reproduces exactly the energy spectrum, global operator algebra, chiral symmetries, and anomalies of the continuum QFT on any finite lattice. Unlike domain wall fermions, truncating the local Hilbert space introduces no extra massless modes, and the entanglement entropy of an interval converges as the truncation is removed. The lattice local algebras are of type I and lie between the type III continuum algebras of nested spatial regions, in accordance with the split property. We demonstrate this construction explicitly for $N$ Majorana fermions, realizing the $\mathrm{O}(N)_\mathrm{L}\times\mathrm{O}(N)_\mathrm{R}$ lattice chiral symmetry. We also construct an exact lattice model for the Schwinger model and numerically reproduce the mass gap $e/\sqrtπ$.

abstracts.value: Gravitational self-force calculations are needed to accurately describe the motion of a small body in a spinning (Kerr) black hole spacetime, which is vital to predict gravitational wave signals from asymmetric-mass compact binaries. Accurate calculations for the upcoming LISA mission require a minimum of second perturbative order in the mass ratio, which has thus far only been achieved for nonspinning (Schwarzschild) black holes due to nonlinear complexities of the Einstein equations. In this work, we calculate Kerr metric perturbations with a new computational approach based on numerical relativity methods, extending recent scalar self-force results to full general relativity. We formulate the perturbative Lorenz-gauge Einstein equations in terms of azimuthal $m$-modes in the frequency domain and solve the resulting elliptic partial differential equations using a spectral discontinuous Galerkin discretization, adaptive mesh refinement, and preconditioned iterative solvers. With our new method, we achieve exponentially convergent first-order gravitational self-force calculations for circular equatorial orbits in Kerr spacetime up to spin $|a|/M=0.998$ (the Thorne limit). Our framework is designed to carry over to second order by delivering accurate and well-behaved first-order data for nonlinear source construction, and as a solver for the second-order metric perturbations themselves.

abstracts.value: Quantum geometry, comprising the Berry curvature (BC) and the quantum metric (QM), underpins a wide array of topological and transport phenomena. However, in most solid-state platforms, BC and QM signals are inherently entangled, making their experimental separation highly challenging. Here, we demonstrate that the chiral limit of type-II semi-Dirac semimetals provides a symmetry-protected mechanism to cleanly isolate the QM. At the chiral limit where the spin-orbit gap $m_z=0$, chiral and $\mathcal{PT}$ symmetries strictly suppress the BC, its dipole (BCD), and the shift current, leaving the QM and its dipole (QMD) as the sole sources of the optical and nonlinear Hall responses. This pure-QM regime exhibits distinct experimental fingerprints, including a divergent longitudinal optical conductivity and a QMD-induced nonlinear Hall conductivity that exhibits a pronounced singularity as the chemical potential approaches the nodal point. Turning on a finite $m_z$ reactivates the BC channels, transitioning the system from a pure-QM phase into a mixed geometric phase. By deriving a scaling law for the nonlinear Hall conductivity, we establish a direct experimental strategy to separate the mixed Drude, BCD, and QMD contributions based on their distinct relaxation-time dependencies. Our findings identify chiral type-II semi-Dirac semimetals as highly tunable platforms for isolating and probing intrinsic quantum geometric effects.

abstracts.value: In recent years, hybrid semiconductor–superconductor qubits have emerged as a compelling alternative to more traditional qubit platforms, owing to their unique combination of material properties and device-level tunability. A key feature of these systems is their gate-tunable Josephson coupling, which enables the realization of superconducting qubit architectures with full electric field control and which offers a promising route toward scalable and low-crosstalk quantum processors. One of the central motivations behind this approach is the possibility of unifying the advantages of superconducting and spin-based qubits. This approach to creating hybrid qubits can be achieved, for example, by encoding quantum information in the spin degree of freedom of a quasiparticle occupying an Andreev bound state, thereby combining long coherence times with fast and flexible control. Recent progress has been further accelerated by the bottom-up engineering of Andreev bound states into coupled quantum dot arrays, leading to the realization of novel device architectures such as minimal Kitaev chains hosting (poor man’s) Majorana states, precursors of topologically protected Majorana zero modes, and, very recently, to the first coherent control of a Majorana parity qubit. In parallel, alternative strategies have focused on the design of Hamiltonian-protected hybrid qubits, including Cooper pair parity qubits and fluxon parity qubits, which aim to enhance robustness against local noise and decoherence. These approaches leverage the interplay between superconducting phase dynamics and the discrete charge or flux degrees of freedom in hybrid junctions. In this article, we review recent theoretical and experimental advances in the development of semiconductor–superconductor hybrid qubits. We provide a comprehensive overview of the underlying physical mechanisms, device implementations, and emerging architectures, with particular emphasis on their potential to enable (topologically) protected quantum information processing. While many of these qubit designs remain at the proof-of-concept stage, the rapid pace of progress suggests that practical demonstrations may be within reach in the near future.

titles.title: Novel qubits in hybrid semiconductor–superconductor nanostructures

abstracts.value: We show that in quantum electrodynamics the Green’s functions of the Dirac-dressed fermion coincide, for any value of the gauge parameter in the <math display="inline"><msub><mi>R</mi><mi>ξ</mi></msub></math> gauge and to all orders in perturbation theory, with those of the undressed fermion in the Landau gauge. The dressed fermion couples only to the transverse photon, and the gauge parameter is confined to a decoupled sector. The dressed vertex then obeys a homogeneous Ward identity, and the dressed field is renormalized multiplicatively with no new counterterm. A partially dressed family realizes the Landau-Khalatnikov-Fradkin relation exactly, and dressings with other kernels reproduce other gauges. Every dressing yields the same pole mass, and assigning the off-shell differences between dressings to the vertex defines a common gauge-invariant mass function.

titles.title: Gauge-invariant fermion

abstracts.value: We investigate an extension of perfect spin hydrodynamics that includes dissipation in the spin sector. The presence of dissipation implies that antisymmetric parts of the energy-momentum tensor should be taken into account. Their form follows from the Navier-Stokes or Israel-Stewart theory, which introduces a priori unknown kinetic coefficients and relaxation times. We find that the inclusion of the antisymmetric parts of the energy-momentum tensor has twofold effects: i) they form source terms for the spin tensor allowing for the transfer between the spin and orbital parts of the total angular momentum (spin-orbit interaction) and ii) they appear in the conservation laws for the energy and linear momentum, indirectly affecting the spin dynamics. Numerical results are obtained for two boost-invariant expansion geometries: one-dimensional longitudinal motion (Bjorken model) and two-dimensional boost-invariant and cylindrically symmetric expansion. They indicate (for various choices of the spin kinetic coefficients and the relaxation times) that the spin polarization tensor approaches thermal vorticity. We also observe that Israel-Stewart dynamics on the way to local equilibrium approaches first the Navier-Stokes regime. In general, we find that the Israel-Stewart formalism naturally helps to consistently combine the conservation laws for linear and angular momentum, while the Navier-Stokes framework itself can lead to a disruption in the structure of the equations through the inclusion of terms involving derivatives of an order higher than one.

titles.title: Novel hydrodynamic features in dissipative spin-polarized fluids

abstracts.value: Direct photons escape heavy-ion collisions with little rescattering, carrying information from the full emission history. Yet describing the measured direct-photon yield and the sizable elliptic flow $v_2$ together remains a long-standing challenge. Here we explore how correlations between emitting partons may affect both observables. The local $2\to2$ photon rate depends on the joint distribution of incoming partons, so a connected correlation between them can change photon emission without changing the one-particle distribution of medium particles. Once folded over the evolving medium in Au+Au and Pb+Pb collisions, the correlation raises the photon yield toward the fitted PHENIX and ALICE data and increases $v_2$ mainly at intermediate $p_T$. The fitted temperature dependence accounts for most of the net flow increase in this region, suggesting that the correlation changes the relative contributions between hotter and cooler regions.

titles.title: Effects of Parton Pair Correlations on Direct-Photon Yields and Elliptic Flow in Heavy-Ion Collisions

abstracts.value: We consider synchronous binary Byzantine agreement among $n$ processes connected by authenticated point-to-point classical and quantum channels. The adversary is computationally unbounded, sees all classical information, adaptively corrupts up to $t\le(1/3-\varepsilon)n$ processes, and may suppress messages sent by a process in the round in which it is corrupted. We give a quantum algorithm that solves Byzantine agreement in this model with probability $1$. It uses $O(\log^4 n)$ rounds, $O(n\log^8 n)$ qubits, and $O(n^2\log^8 n)$ classical bits in expectation, with constants depending on $\varepsilon$. This reduces the quantum communication of the protocol of Ben-Or and Hassidim (STOC~2005), which achieves $O(1)$ expected rounds but whose Byzantine coin implementation requires $Ω(n^4\log n)$ qubits and classical bits. We also extend the quadratic message lower bound of Abraham et al. (PODC~2019) to quantum channels, obtaining an $Ω(t^2)$ lower bound on worst-case expected total communication. For $t=Θ(n)$, the communication and round complexity of our algorithm are therefore optimal up to polylogarithmic factors.

titles.title: Fast Quantum Byzantine Agreement with Nearly Linear Quantum Communication

abstracts.value: Quantifying selection effects in gravitational-wave population studies requires millions of costly signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) calculations. We present $Φ$asmaNet, a compact neural architecture for structured tabular regression, with staged spectral refinement as an explicit architectural prior. Learned input tokens are refined through ordered attention-based $Φ$-Stages, each augmented by a $Φ$-Refractor subspace-mixing module, then revisited through gated top-down $Φ$-Feedback. Applied to the 11-dimensional parameters of precessing, higher-mode binary black hole signals (IMRPhenomXPHM), it predicts phase-averaged optimal SNR for a single detector at fixed Advanced LIGO design sensitivity. With approximately 732k parameters, it outperforms MLP, 1D-ResNet and Transformer-encoder baselines under matched training across $10^5$--$10^6$ samples. At $10^6$ samples, it achieves $100-\mathrm{MAPE}=98.73\%$ on the held-out test set, $99.29\%$ after rank-preserving monotonic (PCHIP) calibration, and $99.39\%$ ($R^2=0.9998$) in the detection-relevant regime $ρ>8$, with stable accuracy across independent dataset realizations. On a single GPU, it sustains approximately $1.2\times10^5$ SNR evaluations per second and processes a $10^6$-injection catalogue end-to-end in approximately 8.3 s, about two orders of magnitude faster than conventional waveform-and-inner-product calculations on a 16-core CPU. Exact distance rescaling through $ρ\propto1/d_L$ supports repeated catalogue-wide detectability evaluations. The fully documented pipeline is intended as a reproducible benchmark, while results on public tabular datasets indicate competitiveness beyond gravitational-wave applications. Although demonstrated for a fixed single-detector configuration, the construction supports extensions to detector networks and epoch-specific sensitivities. (Abridged)

titles.title: $Φ$asmaNet: A Staged Spectral Token-Refinement Architecture for Fast Gravitational-Wave Signal-to-Noise Ratio Prediction

abstracts.value: Many strategies have been proposed to manipulate and protect symmetric quantum correlations against decoherence. However, more research is needed to focus on asymmetric correlations, such as quantum steering. To address this gap, we investigate the dynamics of quantum steering between two moving qubits within separate cavities. Specifically, we explore how the qubits' velocity impacts the dynamics of quantum steering. The results indicate that when each qubit interacts independently with its cavity, increasing its velocity can enhance quantum steering, regardless of whether the dynamics is Markovian or non-Markovian. We also find that the qubits' motion can effectively control the asymmetric nature of steering even when symmetric environmental noise acts on an initially asymmetric mixed state. Furthermore, we analyze the asymmetric properties of quantum steering by considering a scenario in which one qubit remains stationary in its cavity. The findings show that adjusting the velocity of the moving qubit can efficiently manipulate asymmetric properties, such as "one-way" and "two-way" steering, thereby enhancing quantum steering and manipulating its asymmetry without consuming external quantum resources in the cavities.

titles.title: Effect of qubit's motion on quantum steering in leaky cavities

abstracts.value: Employee attrition is a costly operational risk marked by class imbalance and asymmetric misclassification costs. We study a cost-sensitive, gate-based Quantum-enhanced Support Vector Machine (Q-SVM) with class-dependent box constraints, implemented as a data re-uploading fidelity kernel and evaluated by exact statevector simulation with a depolarizing sensitivity check. We state three assumption-bound theoretical results: a convergence rate for cost-weighted kernel-target-alignment optimization under a weighted Polyak-Łojasiewicz condition; a reproducing-kernel-Hilbert-space margin bound that holds under an explicit disjoint-convex-hull separation hypothesis; and a high-probability Nyström error bound with a stratified minority-block scaling estimate in which all sampling factors are retained. On the IBM HR Analytics benchmark ($N{=}1{,}470$, attrition ${\approx }16\%$), evaluated by repeated ($5{\times }3$) nested stratified cross-validation with all metrics computed from saved prediction vectors, the Q-SVM reaches a minority-class recall of 0.571, on a par with classical SVM kernels on the same features, while gradient-boosted trees lead on threshold-free metrics. A methodological finding of independent interest emerges from this comparison: threshold metrics on imbalanced data are strongly sensitive to the map from SVM margin to reported score, with recall at a fixed cut differing by more than 0.5 between two standard conventions applied to identical fitted models. We therefore report every threshold metric under both conventions. A factorial ablation attributes the recall regime to cost weighting rather than to the quantum kernel. We further identify the encoding bandwidth as the dominant hyperparameter of the pipeline: tuning it inside the inner loop raises AUC from 0.660 to 0.734 at four qubits and brings the Q-SVM to statistical parity with a tuned classical RBF at matched feature count, although a classical trigonometric map on the same encoding angles matches it in turn, so the gain is attributable to the encoding rather than to the quantum feature space. The principal empirical model is the fixed-kernel Q-SVM; the trainable variant, which the convergence theory describes, is evaluated separately, and a $2\times 2$ factorial localizes the entire cost-sensitivity effect in the SVM decision layer rather than in the kernel. A direct estimate of the RKHS convex-hull distance shows that the separation hypothesis of the margin bound is not satisfied on this benchmark. We frame the study as a feasibility indicator, not a demonstration of quantum advantage, and add calibration, decision-utility, and responsible-use analyses.

titles.title: Cost-sensitive quantum kernels for imbalanced attrition prediction

abstracts.value: Recent advances have aimed to assess both the potential and difficulties surrounding the use of quantum-enhanced models for the exploration of medical image analysis. Due to continuous development, there is a gap in systematic understanding. This systematic review aims to evaluate the studies on QML models based on specific, real-world medical tasks. This paper uses recent literature focusing on quantum and hybrid quantum-classical models applied to images of different medical conditions. Following the SPAR-4-SLR framework, relevant studies published between 2020 and 2026 were identified through searches of PubMed, Elsevier, MedRxiv, arXiv, Google Scholar, and Research Gate. Studies were included if they were published in English, available in full text, and presented at recognized conferences or published in reputable journals, discussed QML, focused on medical image analysis, and provided sufficient technical detail about the QML model, algorithm, or architecture; duplicate studies, non-English publications, and personal or casual blogs were excluded. Of 1,140 studies identified and screened, 16 were included in the final review. The methodology includes analysis of model architectures, challenges, techniques, performance comparisons between classical and quantum- based models. Further areas for improvement are also explored. Quantum machine learning performs well compared to its classical counterpart in detecting complex patterns even with small datasets. Several approaches also highlight potential benefits for patient privacy preservation; however, the challenges related to hard- ware constraints and well-annotated data remain. While QML holds potential, the current evidence is not enough for clinical readiness. Recent research has been used to analyze the performance, current limitations, and future directions needed for the advancement of this field.

titles.title: Systematic review of quantum machine learning in medical image analysis

abstracts.value: Quantum designated-verifier signature (QDVS) is a cryptographic scheme based on quantum mechanics in which a signature can be verified only by a specific designated verifier. Recently, Xin et al. [31 ] proposed a QDVS scheme based on Bell states and claimed that it was secure. However, we demonstrate that their scheme is vulnerable to forgery attacks. To overcome this vulnerability, we propose an improved QDVS scheme utilizing single qubits, a secret random permutation, and unitary operations. Security analysis shows that the proposed scheme satisfies the required designated-verifier security properties while resisting various attacks. Compared with representative QDVS schemes, our scheme requires neither a third party (TP) nor quantum entanglement resources, and achieves a qubit efficiency of $100\%$ with a quantum cost of one qubit per signed bit and only two quantum communication rounds.

titles.title: Improvements on quantum designated-verifier signature based on Bell states

abstracts.value: Image denoising is essential for reliable image analysis, as residual noise degrades both visual quality and downstream machine learning tasks. Quantum Convolutional Autoencoders (QCAE), have been proposed to improve on classical convolutional autoencoders by replacing the latent space with an ansatz circuit inspired by the Quantum Approximate Optimization algorithm (QAOA). Existing studies still set the ansatz depth and the training hyperparameters by hand, so performance rests on trial and error. Building on the QCAE architecture of Kit et al., this study optimizes its hyperparameters with Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO), validated against four alternatives: grey wolf optimizer, the bat algorithm, plain Harris Hawks Optimization (HHO), and an enhanced Harris Hawks variant. The QAOA-inspired ansatz is reimplemented as a differentiable state vector layer, and all five optimizers search an identical four-dimensional hyperparameter space on a reduced binary MNIST denoising benchmark under Gaussian noise. In the primary run, the PSO-searched QCAE achieved the highest mean test SSIM among all configurations, about 72% above the classical CAE baseline. Over five retraining seeds, its selected configuration had the highest mean SSIM and led in at least four of the five seeds. Across four independent repetitions of the whole search, PSO, the grey wolf optimizer and the enhanced Harris hawks variant reached nearly equal mean SSIM, while plain Harris hawks and the bat algorithm were weaker and less stable. An exploratory search with a wider learning-rate range raised the test SSIM of every optimizer by a factor of 1.7 to 3.6. Metaheuristic search therefore benefits QCAE, but the choice of search bounds matters at least as much as the choice of optimizer.

titles.title: Metaheuristic-Optimized Quantum Convolutional Autoencoder for Image Noise Reduction

abstracts.value: We investigate four-dimensional Reissner-Nordström-de Sitter (RN-dS) black holes within the generalized uncertainty principle (GUP) modified membrane model. The conventional membrane model is plagued by an unnatural cutoff that might lack fundamental physical meaning. In this work, we resolve this issue by introducing a natural, quantum-gravity-motivated cutoff derived from the minimal length predicted by the GUP. Using the membrane paradigm, we compute the free energy and entropy of quantum fields confined near the horizon and enforce normalization to the Bekenstein-Hawking entropy. We analytically solve the membrane thickness and show that its positive definiteness is strictly equivalent to the positivity of surface gravity at the event horizon, which in turn supports the validity of WCCC. The model also naturally breaks down at the Planck scale, consistent with the expected limit of semiclassical gravity. Our results reveal a consistent link between quantum-gravity-motivated horizon thermodynamics and the non-degeneracy condition underlying cosmic censorship.

titles.title: Self-consistency of the generalized uncertainty principle modified membrane model and its consistency with the weak cosmic censorship condition in Reissner-Nordström-de Sitter black holes

abstracts.value: The Super Tau-Charm Facility (STCF), with a designed center-of-mass energy range of $2$-$7~\textrm{GeV}$, a peak luminosity exceeding $0.5\times 10^{35}~\textrm{cm}^{-2}\textrm{s}^{-1}$, a total trigger rate of about 400 kHz, and a total data rate of about 30 GB/s, will impose stringent requirements for fast track finding and data reduction and compression algorithms in the High-Level Trigger. Local track segment finding in the Main Drift Chamber (MDC) underpins subsequent segment combination and full track reconstruction, yet high background rates and limited detection efficiency can significantly increase the risk of false triggers and signal loss in pattern matching algorithms. This paper presents a neural-network-assisted framework for constructing binary template libraries used in matrix-based pattern matching for MDC local track segment finding. The framework formulates template construction as a differentiable multi-objective optimization problem, employing a neural network to jointly learn template parameters under multiple constraints. After training, only binary template pairs are exported and deployed into the existing bitwise pattern matching routine, requiring no neural network inference at runtime and thus preserving the deterministic, fast, and parallelizable nature of the online algorithm. Experimental results based on simulation samples demonstrate that, under limited detection efficiency, the resulting template library maintains relatively high signal retention across different transverse momentum ranges and background levels, and can be flexibly tailored to adjust the coverage range according to practical requirements. The proposed approach combines offline neural-network optimization with a deterministic, fast conventional online algorithm, enabling artificial-intelligence-enhanced online data processing in high-luminosity particle collider experiments.

titles.title: Neural-network-assisted binary template optimization for online pattern matching of the STCF main drift chamber

abstracts.value: This work is devoted to study the topological classification of a Kerr-Newman-de Sitter (KNdS) black hole (BH) in bumblebee gravity (BBG) subject to changes in various parameters. Based on generalized free energy techniques coupled with Duan's $\phi $ mapping topological current theory, we find that BH can be separated into different topological classes. Interestingly, our result demonstrates that the existence of a number of horizons in dS spacetime, in particular, we find that both the event horizon and the cosmological horizon carry two zero points with opposite winding numbers, so that each horizon has vanishing total topological number, $W_h=W_c=0$. The winding-number assignment of the two cosmological-horizon defects is reversed relative to the event horizon, and this classification is unchanged by the electric charge Q and the Lorentz-violation parameter L.

abstracts.value: We formulate semiclassical Hawking transport for a one parameter set of generalized Hayward geometries supported by member specific magnetic nonlinear electrodynamic completions, using the established gauge invariant two channel gravitational and electromagnetic perturbation system and its flux normalized transmission matrices. The matrix greybody description retains channel conversion and parity dependence and generates the outgoing occupation covariance without replacing the coupled system by auxiliary scalar channels. In the coupled quadrupolar sector, the luminosity falls by more than two orders of magnitude between <math altimg="si77.svg" display="inline" id="d1e1830"><mi>χ</mi></math> = 0.2 and 0.9, whereas the electromagnetic share rises from 15.5% to 19.8%. The thermally integrated flux is almost entirely carried by the bright greybody eigenchannel. Rotation to the asymptotic gravitational and electromagnetic basis produces a nonzero, basis specified mutual information flux of about 3% of the marginal entropy in the strong core regime; the outgoing gravitational/electromagnetic state remains separable, so this correlation is not an entanglement or information recovery diagnostic. The coarse grained entropy excess over reversible Clausius transfer is nonnegative frequency by frequency and channel by channel. An effective Reissner–Nordström comparison shows that the strong core change in luminosity is dominated by the temperature difference and that most of the channel mutual information is already present in ordinary charged channel mixing. Finally, a kinematic fixed charge quadrupolar sequence develops a cooling bottleneck, while greybody contractivity and the near extremal surface gravity law exclude finite parameter attainment of extremality within that formal sequence. The sequence compares member specific reconstructed completions and is not interpreted as a physical evaporation history in one fixed nonlinear electrodynamic theory. •Hawking transport retains coupled gravitational and electromagnetic conversion.•Quadrupolar luminosity drops by over two orders of magnitude near extremality.•Bright greybody eigenchannels carry almost all thermally weighted radiation.•Mutual information reflects separable charged channel mixing, not entanglement.•Formal quadrupolar fixed charge flow cannot reach extremality in finite time.

titles.title: Matrix valued Hawking transport and channel covariance for magnetically supported generalized Hayward black holes

Abstract
In Large Volume Scenarios, the axio-dilaton and complex-structure F -terms receivenon-vanishing contributions from several subleading effects, some of which have al-ready been extensively studied in the literature [1–5]. For instance, the inverse of thecorrected Kähler metric induces mixing between the axio-dilaton S and the Kähler di-rections Ti. Since DTi

F -terms to acquire non-zero contributions.In this thesis, we investigate a distinct contribution arising from the displacement ofthe axio-dilaton and complex-structure moduli away from their supersymmetric tree-level flux vacuum. Although these fields are conventionally stabilised at leading orderand subsequently treated as frozen in the analysis of Kähler-moduli stabilisation, theperturbative and non-perturbative effects responsible for the Large Volume Scenariogenerate non-vanishing gradients along the (S, za) directions. As a consequence, thefull minimum is shifted by amounts δS and δza.We compute these displacements perturbatively in the large-volume and weak-coupling regime, organising the results according to their parametric scaling in inversepowers of the compactification volumeV and powers of the string coupling gs. We thendetermine how the shifted vacuum modifies the corresponding F -terms. The analysisis first performed in a simplified model with rigid complex-structure and subsequentlyextended to a model containing a dynamical complex-structure modulus.We find that the shift-induced contribution to the complex-structure sector F -termis enhanced by an additional factor of g−1

By contrast, the corresponding contribution to the axio-dilatonF -term is gener-ically of the same parametric order in gs andV−1 as the contributions already discussedin the literature. We also discuss the phenomenological implications of these correc-tions for soft supersymmetry-breaking terms in sequestered LVS scenarios [3]. In partic-ular, while soft terms controlled by F S remain parametrically unchanged, the modifiedcomplex-structure F -terms can lead to parametrically different contributions to scalarmasses in the ultra-local regime and to the masses of hidden RR photini [4].
