abstracts.value: The Hahn-echo time $T_2$ of nitrogen-vacancy (NV$^-$) ensembles in nitrogen-rich diamond follows the empirical relation $T_2\cdot$[N] = 160 $μ$s ppm, and this relation does not depend on the magnetic field between 2 and 30 mT. Cluster-correlation-expansion (CCE) calculations solve the spin dynamics exactly within small groups of spins. When they treat the Overhauser field of the surrounding P1 centres, that is, the field that these electron spins produce, as frozen, they overestimate $T_2$ at high field by up to a factor of two. This excess was recently attributed to additional dark defects. We show that the excess comes mostly from the frozen field. In our model the P1 centres outside each cluster flip-flop in pairs: two centres exchange their spin states and conserve their total $S_z$. Kinetic Monte Carlo generates these events at golden-rule rates, which follow from the dipolar Hamiltonian without adjustable parameters, and each cluster evolves in the resulting time-dependent field. This dynamical mean field lies between the static-mean-field and mean-field-free limits. For a $^{14}$N P1 bath it reduces $T_2\cdot$[N] at 30 mT from 264 $\pm$ 16 to 188 $\pm$ 12 $μ$s ppm and gives 167 $\pm$ 11 $μ$s ppm at 10 mT, 1.7 and 0.4 standard deviations from experiment, with no dark spins. When each centre jumps independently, $T_2\cdot$[N] is 147 $\pm$ 9 $μ$s ppm at 30 mT; the correlation of the flip-flop partners thus lengthens $T_2$ by 20-30 percent at high field. The Overhauser field is neither frozen nor averaged out by fast motion: 68-83 percent of its autocorrelation survives 200 $μ$s. At 2.5 mT, where the P1 electron and nucleus hybridise, $T_2$ stays below experiment for any choice of rates. Part of the field dependence therefore remains: $T_2$ rises by a factor 1.69 $\pm$ 0.07 instead of 2.15 $\pm$ 0.08 from 2.5 to 30 mT.

titles.title: Dynamical-mean-field cluster-correlation expansion of NV$^-$ spin-echo decoherence in a realistic substitutional-nitrogen bath

abstracts.value: Tidal disruption events (TDEs) can reach super-Eddington luminosities near their peak. While their optical/UV emission may arise from multiple processes, X-rays are more likely to be produced by the innermost accretion flow close to the black hole, analogous to super-Eddington flows in stellar-mass X-ray binaries (XRBs) and active galactic nuclei (AGNs). Super-Eddington AGNs typically show disc-dominated spectra, with weak and steep coronae, while super-Eddington XRBs show a wider variety of spectral shapes. Here we explore disc-corona coupling in TDEs by developing a super-Eddington ($\dot{m}>1$: slim) disc model in which magnetic reconnection transfers some of the accretion power from the disc into a hot Comptonizing corona. We test the model on the well-monitored X-ray TDE AT2021ehb, and can broadly fit the brightest X-ray spectra with a black-hole mass $M_{\rm BH}\sim10^6$--$10^7\,M_\odot$ at $\dot m\sim 1$, but need variable magnetic coupling to the disc to match the large observed fast changes in coronal contribution. AGN at similarly high luminosity do not show such variable coronae, but the transient XRB outbursts do, suggesting that it may be a common feature of rapidly changing, non-steady accretion flows. As the TDE declines to $\dot{m}\sim 0.01$, the source hardens, but never goes below $Γ\sim 2$, unlike both AGN and XRB at these luminosities. Thus the X-ray spectral evolution in this TDE does not resemble either XRB or AGN in detail, likely pointing to the very different, highly variable nature of the accretion flow in a tidal disruption event.

titles.title: A magnetically heated slim disc-corona model for tidal disruption events

abstracts.value: We show that, within covariant Hamiltonian gravity in spherical symmetry, a prescribed one-parameter family of static vacuum geometries uniquely determines the local dynamics of gravitational collapse coupled to irrotational dust, despite the nonuniqueness of the underlying gravitational Hamiltonian. We further derive necessary and sufficient conditions under which the resulting dynamics admits a homogeneous and isotropic cosmological sector. These conditions establish a two-way correspondence between static vacuum geometries and modified Friedmann dynamics and impose a universal restriction on the spatial-curvature dependence of the latter. Our results provide a criterion for determining whether independently proposed black-hole and cosmological models can arise from a common covariant gravitational theory.

abstracts.value: In solid-state physics, the ability to open and tune an electronic energy gap provides a direct route to controlling charge transport and accessing distinct electronic phases. In solids with physical boundaries, a bulk energy gap formed exclusively by extended bulk states is conventionally expected to be governed primarily by the interior bulk region, with only a minor contribution from the boundaries. Here we show that, in stark contrast to this conventional expectation, the bulk gap of armchair graphene nanoribbons in the $N_w=3p+2$ family with $p\in\mathbb{Z}\ge 0$ can be fully controlled through the hoppings solely at the boundaries. This full boundary control originates from an exact cancellation between the gap contributions of long-range hoppings along and across the ribbon in the bulk region. It persists in the presence of Hubbard interactions and holds irrespective of ribbon width in this family. Our findings establish boundary dynamics as an unexpectedly powerful means of manipulating bulk electronic properties, enabling width-preserving engineering of one-dimensional (1D) band structures and topological phases, with potential applications in qubits, artificial quantum spin chains, topological quantum dots and other quantum devices.

titles.title: Full edge control of bulk energy gap in armchair graphene nanoribbons

abstracts.value: Transition-edge sensors (TESs) exploit the resistive transition of a superconductor to detect minute changes in temperature. While significant progress has been made in understanding the temperature- and current-dependent resistive transition in these devices, important aspects of TES behavior under bias remain unresolved. In particular, existing TES models largely neglect spatial variations in the superconducting state and current distribution arising from device geometry and proximity effects associated with the superconducting leads and normal metal features. Using scanning superconducting quantum interference device (SQUID) microscopy (SSM), we directly image local superconducting properties and transport current in two molybdenum-gold (MoAu) X-ray TES designs. We measure the local diamagnetic response to identify superconducting regions in devices voltage-biased within the transition and the Oersted field generated by the transport current to reconstruct the corresponding current distribution. We observe bias-dependent reconfigurations of the current distribution that track current-induced changes in superconducting regions, highlighting the importance of mesoscale spatial variations for TES device physics, operation, and design.

titles.title: Imaging the Current Distribution in Superconducting Transition-Edge Sensors with Scanning SQUID Microscopy

abstracts.value: Explicit quantum circuits for the acoustic and elastic wave equations, obtained by Hamiltonian simulation of their first-order forms, conserve energy and therefore describe closed domains: an outgoing wave reflects off the edge of the computational region or, with periodic boundaries, wraps around and re-enters from the opposite side. We open the domain with the simplest physical absorber, a graded sponge layer in which every wave field is damped at a rate that grows towards the outer edge, and implement the resulting dissipative dynamics on a quantum simulator by Schrödingerisation, which turns a non-unitary linear evolution into a family of unitary ones by means of a single auxiliary variable. We derive the whole chain from the partial differential equation to the circuit, in one, two and three dimensions. An independent finite-difference solver confirms that damping all wave fields absorbs far better than the common velocity-only damping mask. For the sponge the quantum analysis is sharp: recovery is exact on the whole non- negative half of the auxiliary axis at every time; that axis can be truncated periodically at a length set by the largest damping rate and the simulated time; and the success probability is a fixed constant, about 0.4, times the fraction of the energy not yet absorbed, with only one or two auxiliary qubits measured. On the circuit side, the damping step, which generic synthesis compiles into a number of controlled-NOT gates exponential in the number of qubits, factorises exactly into polynomially many multi-controlled phase gates. Gate-level simulations on up to 25 qubits agree with the classical solutions of the damped wave equations.

titles.title: Quantum simulation of dissipative acoustic and elastic waves by Schrödingerisation: absorbing boundaries and explicit polynomial-size circuits

abstracts.value: Signatures of the presence of quark matter inside neutron stars are obtained from the analysis of more than 250,000 mass-radius curves that describe nucleonic, hyperonic and hybrid stars, based on five different hadronic relativistic mean-field models and four different descriptions of quark matter. A radius maximum occurring above $1.7\,M_\odot$ strongly favors quark matter inside the star. A second criterion identifying the presence of quark matter is $X>-0.2$km, where X=[R(2.0)-R(1.6)]-[R(1.6)-R(1.4)] is obtained from the radius of stars with 2.0, 1.6 and 1.4 $M_\odot$. It is also shown that most of the hyperonic stars have a radius maximum that peaks around 1.5$M_\odot$ and compactness below 0.27 for the maximum-mass configuration, while for the nucleonic stars that have a radius maximum, this peaks below 1.3$M_\odot$ and the compactness of the maximum-mass configuration lies above 0.26.

titles.title: Signatures of quark matter from neutron star mass-radius curve

abstracts.value: We report the detection of two single dispersed pulses with widths of about 6.7 ms and 15.6 ms and flux densities of about 0.8 and 1.7 Jy. These were found in a blind survey of two circular regions (Dec$\;=+22^{\circ}$ and $+5^{\circ}$,RA: 0--24~h) at high radio frequencies \mbox{(4400--5000\,MHz)} using four 4-channel filter radiometers (central frequencies of 4475, 4625, 4775, and 4925 MHz) spanning a total frequency bandwidth of 600 MHz. The survey was carried out with the Western Sector antenna of the RATAN-600 radio telescope, which had an effective area of 1200 m$^2$ in~2017--2025. The total area of the survey was about 1500~square degrees, and each pointing of the antenna lasted one year. We consider these to be two rare, high-frequency FRB events (MJD~58614.38257 and MJD~58659.62482), detected with estimated dispersion measures of $200\pm20$ and $266\pm10$ pc cm$^{-3}$ at a final signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) level of 8--9 after additional optimal filtration. After subtraction of the estimated dispersions within the Milky Way, we estimated redshifts of approximately 0.09 and 0.13, respectively, using the traditional equation: ${\rm DM}\,[{\rm pc~cm}^{-3}] = 1000\,z$ for the intergalactic medium. The estimated isotropic energies of the FRBs are equal to $10^{40}$ erg and $2\times 10^{40}$ erg, respectively. To effectively detect single pulses, we applied machine learning methods using a neural network trained on synthetic FRB pulse profiles.

titles.title: Two Fast Radio Burst Candidates Detected in the RATAN-600 Blind Survey

abstracts.value: The neutrinophilic two-Higgs-doublet model ($ν$2HDM) represents one of the most economical extensions of the Standard Model (SM) while still giving rise to a rich phenomenology. In this work, we carry out a full tree-level and one-loop matching of this ultraviolet completion onto the SM Effective Field Theory extended with right-handed neutrinos ($ν$SMEFT), including all operators up to mass dimension six. This is achieved by integrating out the heavy scalar doublet at a scale well above the electroweak scale. For the matching procedure, we employ the functional method in combination with the naive dimensional regularization and modified minimal subtraction schemes. After converting from the Green's basis to the minimal, non-redundant Warsaw-extended basis, the effects of high-scale new physics are encoded in the Wilson coefficients of both physical and evanescent operators in the $ν$SMEFT. These coefficients are given in terms of the $ν$2HDM parameters prior to spontaneous symmetry breaking. Our final expressions at the high-energy matching scale are provided as ancillary files on \href{https://github.com/dufewe/v2HDM-to-vSMEFT}{GitHub}. This setup forms the foundation for forthcoming systematic and global analyses of the $ν$2HDM parameter space using effective field theory techniques.

titles.title: Matching $ν$2HDM onto $ν$SMEFT up to one-loop accuracy

abstracts.value: Quantum state engineering frequently employs non-Gaussian operations, particularly photon addition and subtraction, to tailor and improve the nonclassical characteristics of quantum states. We investigate how photon addition to a two-mode squeezed Fock state (TMSFS) influences its performance in the Braunstein-Kimble quantum teleportation protocol. We obtain the Wigner characteristic function of the photon-added TMSFS (PA-TMSFS) and evaluate the corresponding teleportation fidelities for both Gaussian and non-Gaussian input states. We further compare the teleportation performance of PA-TMSFS with that of its photon-subtracted counterpart by accessing their fidelity enhancements over the parent TMSFS and considering the probabilistic nature of both the operations. Our results demonstrate that photon subtraction provides superior teleportation performance compared with photon addition, with this advantage becoming more pronounced when the success probabilities of the corresponding non-Gaussian operations are considered. In particular, the symmetric $(1,1)$ photon subtraction yields the optimal trade-off between teleportation fidelity and success probability among the configurations investigated. These findings highlight that photon subtraction retains its advantage even when the underlying entangled resource is already non-Gaussian.

titles.title: Quantum teleportation using photon-added two-mode squeezed Fock states: A comparison with photon-subtracted counterparts

abstracts.value: Chemical abundances in the Galactic Centre (GC) are challenging to measure because of high extinction, crowding, and distance, and are typically limited to the brightest AGB and M giants observed in the near-infrared. In contrast, hypervelocity stars (HVSs) ejected from the GC by Sgr A* carry their natal composition into accessible regions such as the Milky Way halo, making them unique probes of GC chemistry. We present high-resolution optical Magellan/MIKE spectroscopy of DESI-312, a bound HVS candidate in the halo with super-solar metallicity ($[\mathrm{Fe/H}]=0.2\pm0.1$). This sets it apart from accreted halo populations on radial orbits and is most naturally explained by GC formation and Hills-mechanism ejection. Updated isochrone fits give an age of 7.4-11.3 Gyr; together with its metallicity and kinematics, this strengthens the case for a GC origin. Korg and Turbospectrum spectral synthesis yields $[\mathrm{X/Fe}]$ for 22 elements, plus Li from an independent line-by-line NLTE analysis. As DESI-312 is near the main sequence, its C, N, and O abundances are unaltered by dredge-up; to our knowledge, these are the first such measurements of unevolved GC material. Its abundance pattern lies where the nuclear star cluster (NSC), nuclear stellar disc (NSD), and inner-bulge sequences overlap, with a Na enhancement ($[\mathrm{Na/Fe}]=+0.16^{+0.03}_{-0.04}$) more modest than in NSC giants of similar metallicity. Chemistry alone thus cannot identify its progenitor; we nevertheless favour the NSC, given its large reservoir of old, metal-rich stars and the star's kinematics. Alongside WINERED-HVS1 and the S-star S0-6/S10, whose abundances point to different progenitors, this tentatively suggests multiple progenitor populations for the S-star cluster. DESI-312 is a test case for sampling GC chemistry with ejected dwarfs at optical wavelengths, complementing near-infrared studies of giants.

titles.title: Chemical abundances of a Galactic Centre ejecta discovered in DESI

abstracts.value: We derive a mass variation identity expressing the first law of black hole thermodynamics for asymptotically flat, stationary, axisymmetric Einstein-Maxwell solutions with multiple electrically charged horizons and finite conical axis singularities. Under the stated asymptotic and parameter regularity hypotheses, the identity holds for independent variations of all parameters within families of fixed horizon types. On the all-degenerate family, a correction to the ADM mass defines a scalar function whose derivatives with respect to angular momenta are the horizon angular velocities. At the Majumdar-Papapetrou family, its angular momentum Hessian is positive definite. Combining the first variation identity with a separate theorem on the sign of the conical parameters shows that this Hessian is nondecreasing in the positive-semidefinite order along admissible paths of increasing Weyl gaps at fixed positive charges.

titles.title: First law of thermodynamics for interacting charged black holes and applications

abstracts.value: The forward matrix elements of the energy-momentum tensor in momentum space, parameterized by gravitational transverse-momentum distributions (TMDs), provide a microscopic window into hadronic mechanical structure. While the longitudinal and transverse columns match to canonical vector TMDs up to twist-4, the light-front minus column involves the unintegrated parton energy $k^-$, leaving this sector undetermined in general quantum chromodynamics. Working within relativistic light-front constituent frameworks where active quarks are modeled as effective on-shell quasiparticles, we show that this energy factorizes algebraically. This establishes a closed matching relating all 32 gravitational TMDs to canonical vector TMDs up to twist-4, including target polarization and T-odd final-state interactions. This completion provides access to the light-front energy density and its transverse Sivers dipole distortion, demonstrates the local equivalence between convective energy and momentum transport velocities, and determines the longitudinal normal stress. Comparing longitudinal and transverse stresses yields a boost-invariant anisotropy ratio that charts the mechanical crossover from collinear confinement dominance to transverse isotropic balance. While formulated within the constituent approximation, these results offer baseline insights into the three-dimensional continuum mechanics of the nucleon.

titles.title: On-shell constituent approach to the light-front partonic energy-momentum tensor

abstracts.value: We present two efficient shell-model approaches for calculating nuclear matrix elements (NMEs) for two-neutrino double-beta ($2νββ$) decay and two-neutrino double-electron capture ($2ν$ECEC), based on the Lanczos strength-function and block-Lanczos techniques. The dual-sided Lanczos strength-function (DLSF) and block-Lanczos strength-function (BLSF) methods avoid the explicit calculation of a complete set of exact intermediate $1^+$ eigenstates and yield fully converged NMEs with a relatively small number of iterations starting from Gamow--Teller (GT) doorway states. Both methods simultaneously preserve the total GT strengths associated with the initial and final nuclei. We benchmark the methods for $^{48}$Ca in the $fp$ shell and apply them to candidates in different mass regions, including $^{58}$Ni, $^{76}$Ge, and $^{130}$Te. For $^{48}$Ca, a calculation allowing cross-shell excitations of up to $2\hbarω$ in the $sdpf$ model space yields a $2νββ$ NME closer to the experimental estimate than the result obtained in the $fp$ shell. For $^{58}$Ni, we present, to our knowledge, the first shell-model calculation of the $2νβ^+$EC/$2ν$ECEC NME. Comparison with the current experimental upper limit on the NME indicates the need for a more sensitive measurement of the $2νβ^+$EC half-life. As an independent validation, the energy-denominator-free sums obtained with the proposed methods are compared with the corresponding double-GT matrix elements calculated directly between the initial and final ground states. Their agreement demonstrates that the methods correctly recover the complete energy-denominator-free intermediate-state sums.

titles.title: Evaluation of $2νββ$ decay nuclear matrix elements using Lanczos techniques preserving Gamow-Teller strengths from both parent and daughter nuclei

abstracts.value: A programmable quantum processor implements a target unitary using information stored in a classical or quantum program register. For arbitrary unitaries in $\mathrm{SU}(d)$, quantum programs attain the optimal leading-order memory cost, whereas deterministic classical rounding requires twice as much memory for the same diamond-distance error. We show that this gap disappears when classical randomization is allowed. We introduce barycentric programming, which stores the label of a unitary randomly selected from a finite set, with probabilities chosen so that first-order approximation errors cancel in the averaged unitary channel. Consequently, the diamond-distance error scales quadratically with the discretization spacing. For any $ν$-parameter family of unitaries forming a compact, smooth manifold without boundary, this method achieves error $\varepsilon$ using only $(ν/2)\log_2(1/\varepsilon)+O(1)$ classical bits. We also prove a matching lower bound for arbitrary quantum programs, determining the optimal leading-order program size for general unitary families. Thus, classical randomization achieves the optimal scaling $(ν/2+o(1))\log_2(1/\varepsilon)$ without requiring coherent quantum memory.

titles.title: Barycentric programming: Classical realization of programs for universal quantum processors

abstracts.value: We present the timing solution of the millisecond pulsar PSR J1657-0406A in the globular cluster M10, based on observations performed with the Five-hundred-meter Aperture Spherical radio Telescope (FAST). The timing results show that PSR J1657-0406A is in a long-period ($P_b \sim 37$ days) and eccentric ($e \sim 0.12$) orbit. We also measured the periastron advance $\dotω = 0.00090(13)$ degrees per year, which implies a total system mass of $2.5(6)$ solar masses, assuming that general relativity accurately models the orbital motion. No optical counterpart was detected within the positional uncertainty, indicating that the companion is unlikely to be a main-sequence star. Considering possible formation channels for the orbital eccentricity, we favor a helium white dwarf companion, although a massive white dwarf or neutron star cannot be completely excluded.

titles.title: A Massive and Eccentric Binary Millisecond Pulsar in the Globular Cluster M10

abstracts.value: Zero-noise extrapolation estimates ideal quantum observables by amplifying noise and extrapolating the measured response. Its accuracy depends on whether the extrapolation model captures the physical effect of amplification, including correlations between repeated operations. Here we derive the response of complete multiqubit gate folding in the simultaneous presence of time-local Markovian noise and stationary finite-band 1/f noise. An ordered circuit kernel couples the observable to noise memory; exact block counting shows how folding samples correlations at increasing time separations. The resulting response contains an r^2 ln r coordinate, with a coefficient fixed by the noise spectrum and the integrated forward-inverse control response. Ordinary polynomial Richardson extrapolation leaves a calculable contribution from this coordinate; the three-node rule (1,3,5) retains 2.73 theta. We construct response-matched extrapolation, including a log-domain implementation, that cancels this contribution at the retained order. Explicit bounds separate the remaining control-shape, finite-band, higher-order, and native-offset errors. The theory applies to arbitrary finite multiqubit circuits within the stated control and noise model, and distinguishes removal of memory-induced bias from an unconditional guarantee of the ideal intercept. Single- and ten-qubit numerical examples illustrate the predicted correction and its response dependence.

titles.title: Logarithmic Bias of Zero-Noise Extrapolation under 1/f Noise

abstracts.value: A unified framework for track reconstruction in the ACTAR Time Projection Chamber (ACTAR TPC) is presented, designed to address the specific challenges of direct-reaction and resonance-elastic scattering experiments involving exotic nuclei. The actroot software package enables efficient semi-online analysis by integrating a continuity-based clustering algorithm followed by a modular filtering procedure to reduce noise, delta-electron contamination, and track fragmentation. The software was benchmarked with experimental data taken with a secondary 20O beam delivered by the LISE3 spectrometer at GANIL. The algorithm achieves reconstruction efficiencies exceeding 90% across various event topologies. The system provides accurate particle identification and reaction-point determination, facilitating the extraction of key physical observables. These results demonstrate the framework's suitability for its application to direct reaction experiments in cubic active-target TPCs without magnetic fields.

titles.title: Track reconstruction with ACTAR TPC: a transfer-reaction use case

abstracts.value: We investigate the strong coupling form factors associated with the $NNρ$ interaction vertex in nuclear matter using the QCD sum rule framework. These form factors are calculated incorporating the in-medium modifications of the relevant condensates and operators into the operator product expansion (OPE) for the first time. We analyze the behavior of the strong form factors as functions of the momentum transfer squared and density of medium and evaluate the corresponding strong couplings at the on-shell point of the $ρ$ meson at nuclear saturation density. Then we extend the analyses to get information at higher densities. Our results provide complementary information on the in-medium $NNρ$ interaction and may be useful for phenomenological, experimental and observational studies of dense hadronic matter.

titles.title: Strong vertex $N N ρ$ in dense medium

abstracts.value: We consider generalized de Sitter entropy which includes both entanglement entropy of the strongly coupled quantum field and the gravitational Wald entropy in the framework of holographic semiclassical gravity. The quantum corrected de Sitter spacetime is constructed perturbatively by considering static deformations of the classical solution. By applying the Noether charge formula to our semiclassical model, we show that both the renormalized entropies remain finite without introducing a cutoff, even when the bulk AdS gravitational field does not satisfy the Dirichlet boundary condition. We show that the first order variation of the generalized entropy with respect to the de Sitter horizon always vanishes when the conformal boundary metric is promoted to a dynamical variable.

titles.title: The generalized entropy in holographic semiclassical de Sitter spacetime

abstracts.value: We analyze the gravitational-wave (GW) signal produced by a relativistic magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) simulation of a short GRB jet with parameters corresponding to those of GRB 170817A. The signal that is generated in the hidden central engine of the GRBs is computed by direct integration of the retarded solution of the linearized Einstein equations of an MHD simulation. Separating the GW signal into its baryonic and electromagnetic contributions, we identify the physical origin of its dominant features. The waveform is of the memory type, with $h(f) \propto 1/f$ at low frequencies and a knee at $\sim 0.5-0.5$Hz set by the energy injection time, which corresponds to the GRB duration. A pronounced early peak reflects the opening of the magnetic field lines and the equatorial kick given to the ejecta at the onset of the jet, demonstrating that the GW signal can reveal processes deep in the GRB engine that cannot be observed otherwise. The signal is strongest for observers far from the jet axis. The total radiated GW energy is only $\sim 10^{42}$ erg, about $10^{-9}$ of the jet energy; it scales as ${\cal E}^2/τ$ with the shortest variability time $τ$, so this is a lower limit. Comparing the predicted spectrum with the sensitivity of current and future detectors, we find that events similar to GW170817 are marginally detectable by DECIGO from up to 10 Mpc and by the Einstein Telescope from 1 Mpc. The injected Poynting flux in this simulation was smooth. An engine variable on a millisecond timescale, as predicted in some GRB models, would substantially increase the GW energy and detectability.

titles.title: Gravitational-Wave Signal from a Short GRB Relativistic MHD Jet

abstracts.value: According to the Festina Lente bound, particles charged under a $U(1)$ gauge field cannot be too light. Otherwise, the largest charged black holes of de Sitter space would discharge in a way that leads to a crunching singularity in violation of cosmic censorship. The Festina Lente bound has previously been extended to also include a background of thermal radiation, but where vacuum energy still dominates cosmic evolution, which imposes a maximal temperature $T\leq T_{\max}=(cV/σ)^{1/4}$. We extend this analysis by accounting for thermal enhancement of the discharge process and making the analysis more quantitative. The result is a bound $m\gtrsim\ell (cV/σ)^{1/4}$ on the masses of charged particles. Here, $\ell$ is a term that depends logarithmically on the gauge coupling and particle charge. At weak coupling this leads to a significantly stronger constraint than the $\sqrt{gq}$ scaling of the original Festina Lente bound. As a result, the present vacuum energy requires every particle of charge $10^{-26}\lesssim gq\lesssim e$ to be heavier than $0.03$--$0.2$ eV, provided its gauge boson is lighter than the Hubble scale. An unbroken gauged $B-L$ with Dirac neutrinos gives $m_{ν,{\rm lightest}}\gtrsim10$--$43$ meV for $10^{-29}\lesssim g_{B-L}\lesssim10^{-24}$, in tension with the DESI DR2 limit once $g_{B-L}\gtrsim7\times10^{-28}$. The same limit bounds a neutrino millicharge to $ε_ν\lesssim2\times10^{-27}$. We also revisit the Standard Model effective field theory constraints from the electroweak phase transition. During slow-roll inflation the Standard Model electron violates the bound over the whole range of Hubble rates allowed by the CMB tensor limit and by nucleosynthesis, unless the photon is Higgsed, its coupling is suppressed, or one considers very fine-tuned versions of Higgs inflation.

titles.title: Thermal Festina Lente

abstracts.value: Stellar feedback plays a key role in regulating star formation and shaping the evolution of star-forming galaxies. Low-mass galaxies provide one of the most powerful laboratories for testing stellar feedback and its impact on galaxy evolution. Numerical simulations predict that repeated feedback-driven gas inflows and outflows generate a "breathing mode," producing a positive correlation between mass-normalized gas velocity dispersion and recent star formation in dwarf galaxies. Whether this kinematic signature persists at higher stellar masses has remained untested. We investigate this question using $\sim1200$ star-forming galaxies with Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI) spectroscopy and COSMOS2020 photometry spanning $7.9<\log M_\star/M_\odot<11.5$ within $z<0.25$. Ionized-gas kinematics are measured with pPXF, and recent star formation histories are reconstructed through joint spectrophotometric fitting with Prospector. We confirm the predicted positive correlation throughout the low-mass regime with $\log M_\star/M_\odot \lesssim 9.8$, quantitatively consistent with previous observations and FIRE-2 simulations. Above $\log M_\star/M_\odot \sim 9.8$, the correlation weakens rapidly and becomes consistent with zero, providing the first empirical constraint on the stellar mass scale above which the kinematic signature of feedback-driven outflow cycles becomes negligible. Our results establish a characteristic stellar mass above which stellar feedback no longer dominates galaxy-scale gas kinematics, providing a new observational benchmark for models of feedback-regulated galaxy evolution. Future joint analyses of gas kinematics and stellar structure will test whether this transition is accompanied by the broader galaxy response predicted by the breathing mode scenario.

titles.title: The Stellar-Mass Dependence of Feedback-Driven Outflows in DESI DR1 Star-Forming Galaxies

abstracts.value: We present the results for the hadron spectrum, the pseudoscalar meson decay constants, and the quark mass ratio in the continuum limit using the ``PACS10'' gauge configurations generated with the $O(a)$-improved Wilson quark action and the Iwasaki gauge action. Numerical simulations are carried out at three lattice spacings keeping the space-time volumes over (10 fm$)^4$ in 2+1 flavor QCD at the physical point. We calculate physical quantities with two choices of conventions to define pseudoexperimental values expected in the isosymmetric QCD. In order to investigate the finite size effects on the physical quantities we have additionally generated the (5.4 fm$)^4$ lattice at the coarsest lattice spacing of $a=0.08487(14)$~fm, which is a hypercube with half the length in each direction compared to the PACS10 configurations. While the finite size effect is hardly observed in comparison of the hadron effective masses on the (10.9 fm$)^4$ and (5.4 fm$)^4$ lattices, the results for the pseudoscalar meson decay constants show discrepancies beyond the error bars. The (5.4 fm$)^4$ lattice also serves for determining the expansion parameters of the pseudoscalar meson masses and decay constants, and the octet baryon masses in terms of the quark masses around the physical point with the aid of the mass reweighting technique. The expansion parameters are used for the fine-tuning of the physical point employing the pseudoexperimental masses of the $π$ meson, $K$ meson, and the $Ξ$ baryon as physical inputs in each convention. We compare the results for the octet baryon masses and the pseudoscalar decay constants in the continuum limit with the corresponding pseudoexperimental values in both conventions. We also discuss the deviation between two results with different conventions. As for the quark mass ratio the result is compared with the recent FLAG summary.

abstracts.value: Homodyne breeding is a promising optical route for generating large cat states and Gottesman--Kitaev--Preskill (GKP) grid states, using readily available squeezed-cat states as inputs. We analyze the performance of protocols, using squeezed single-photon seeds, $\hat{S}(r)\ket{1}$, as squeezed-cat resources and propagating them through the same cat-to-GKP breeding pipeline. For a symmetric tree with $N=2^{m_1}$ seeds, the heralded resource state reduces to a state with a polynomial-Gaussian wavefunction controlled by a single effective width, achieving near-unit fidelity with the desired cat resource state. Our analysis yields closed-form even-cat fidelities and an inverse-design rule for the seed squeezing. We apply these resources to GKP breeding, and find a large overlap with a practical GKP state. We also investigate the effects of practical imperfections, including finite homodyne acceptance windows and photon loss. This study shows that squeezed single-photon inputs provide a viable resource assignment for homodyne cat and GKP breeding, replacing the demanding requirement for high-resolution photon-number-resolving heralding with an on-demand single-photon source.

titles.title: Performance analysis of cat and GKP breeding protocols with squeezed single-photon input

abstracts.value: Extreme mass ratio inspirals on inclined orbits can produce recurrent electromagnetic flares by shocking gas at accretion-disk crossings. Using forward ray tracing in Kerr spacetime, we investigate how self-lensing by the central supermassive black hole (SMBH) reshapes these flares. Flares emitted behind the SMBH can be strongly magnified, whereas near-side flares remain almost unmagnified, producing strong-weak alternation even for identical intrinsic emission. As Lense-Thirring precession shifts the crossing azimuths, it generates long-term amplitude envelopes whose spacing can be used to infer the precession period. Lense-Thirring precession can also increase the cumulative geometric lensing probability over longer observing windows. Within individual flares, Keplerian motion of hotspots co-rotating with the disk produces time-dependent magnification, which can generate shoulders or double peaks and change the effective width. We also propose a spectral diagnostic to distinguish self-lensing from external lensing when their light curves are similar: self-lensing can amplify later, cooler emission and produce a softer secondary peak, whereas delayed images from a static external lens repeat the same intrinsic spectral evolution.

titles.title: Self-lensing of electromagnetic counterparts to extreme mass ratio inspirals

abstracts.value: We discuss the formation of trapped surfaces induced by short pulses of incoming gravitational radiation and matter fields, in a double-null formulation. We identify a hierarchy of orders in the pulse width for the geometric and matter quantities consistent with the evolution equations. Under the assumption that this hierarchy holds throughout the region considered, the incoming fluxes undergo approximately conservative inward transport and are thereby amplified. The Raychaudhuri equation then gives an initial flux criterion for trapped surface formation. The conditions on the matter are expressed through the Ricci components and their derivatives, which allows the argument to be developed without specifying a particular matter model.

abstracts.value: We demonstrate the use of a superconducting mixer for direct searches for dark photon dark matter (DPDM) in the meV mass range. DPDM couples to the ordinary electromagnetic field through kinetic mixing with a coupling constant $χ$ and can convert into ordinary photons at the surface of a metal plate. For DPDM masses of 1 meV, the conversion photons have frequencies of around 240 GHz. At such frequencies, superconducting mixers enable low-noise spectroscopic measurements. We performed a direct search for DPDM in the mass range 1.0047578-1.0047598 meV, corresponding to the frequency range 242.94935-242.94983 GHz, using approximately one hour of data obtained with a cryogenic millimeter-wave receiver based on a superconducting mixer. No significant excess was found, and we set upper limits of $χ< (1.6\text{-}1.9)\times10^{-9}$ at the 95% confidence level. These limits are comparable to existing constraints from solar dark photons. By applying this method, we plan to extend the search to the wider mass range of 0.7-1.1 meV, corresponding to 170-260 GHz, with improved sensitivity.

abstracts.value: The Dymnikova spacetime replaces the Schwarzschild singularity with a de Sitter core, and its lapse deviates from Schwarzschild by a factor decaying as $e^{-r^3/(2l_{\rm cr}^2M)}$. Whether this screening renders the core invisible to accretion has remained an open quantitative question. We address it with GRHD simulations of BHL accretion onto Dymnikova BH for six values of the critical length, $0.1M\le l_{\rm cr}\le 1.1M$, the last being 97% of the extremal value. All runs share identical gas parameters and resolution, so any difference in the flow must originate from the geometry. The dynamically relevant quantity is the gravitational acceleration, whose deviation reaches 12% at the inner boundary for the most strongly corrected model, yet the flow responds only locally: the post-shock density drops by 10% in the innermost zone and the quiet-phase accretion rate by 0.12%, with no effect beyond $r\simeq2.7M$. Because runs differing by as little as $\sim 10^{-10}$ in the metric decorrelate completely once the shock-cone instability saturates, we compare models statistically using ensembles of independent realizations. The time-averaged accretion rate is then independent of $l_{\rm cr}$ to within 0.8% $(2σ)$ at all radii; the variability amplitude, shock-cone opening angle $(1.077\pm0.003 rad)$, and stagnation radius $(26.8\pm0.3M)$ vary only within the realization scatter; the propagation lags $(75.5\pm1.0M$ and $31.6\pm0.4M)$ agree to within 1.6%; and no power spectrum carries a detectable core signature. Accretion onto a Dymnikova BH is therefore observationally indistinguishable from accretion onto a Schwarzschild black hole: timing observations test the shock-cone mechanism, not the regular core. More broadly, ensemble-based statistical comparisons are essential before differences between simulated accretion flows in different spacetimes can be interpreted as physical.

titles.title: Hidden by Exponential Screening: The Invisibility of the Dymnikova Black Hole de Sitter Core to Accretion Observables

abstracts.value: We discover that electric charge can activates birefringence for a neutral vector field coupled to the Einstein tensor around a Reissner-Nordström black hole. Changing the electric charge of an uncoupled black hole can mimic one parity's shadow radius of a coupled black hole. The coupling makes the two parity looks differently. It separates their shadow edges of two parities and produces a backward-scattered signal with reversed helicity. However changing the charge alone cannot reproduce both effects. They require both nonzero charge and coupling. At weak coupling, the leading correction is the same for both potential. Positive coupling raises the potential, reduces low-frequency absorption and decrease the average shadow radius. Negative coupling reverses these trends. The backward signal is nonzero, this is due to the difference between the complex scattering amplitudes of the two parities. It is entirely helicity reversed. For the uncoupled field, the shadows is the same for both parities and the backward intensity vanishes exactly at every charge. We can use the split edge and backward signal to distinguish the coupling from a change of charge alone. A comparison with observations still requires a mechanism that produces and detects this field.

titles.title: Charge-Activated Birefringence and Shadow Mimicry around Reissner-Nordström Black Holes

abstracts.value: The two-frequency heating (TFH) method is widely used to improve the performance of electron cyclotron resonance (ECR) ion sources, yet its physical mechanisms remain insufficiently understood. In this work, the TFH regime in the DECRIS-PM ECR ion source is studied numerically using the NAM-ECRIS code. Single-frequency heating at 14.51 GHz (500 W) is compared to two-frequency heating at 14.51 GHz and 13 GHz (450 W + 50 W) at equal total power. It is found that while the global plasma parameters remain largely unchanged, the peak density of highly anisotropic electrons (E > 1 keV, Vperp/Vlong > 10) decreases by ~20% and their distribution broadens radially in the TFH regime. This reduction in electron anisotropy is attributed to the randomizing effect of the lower-frequency wave on electron gyromotion, which suppresses plasma micro-instabilities and leads to improved ion production.

titles.title: Numerical Study of Two-Frequency Heating in ECR Ion Source

abstracts.value: We measure current across a voltage-biased, long array of Josephson junctions. Current-voltage characteristics do not reveal any critical current and instead display the presence of threshold voltage and finite activation energy, consistent with the Coulomb blockade. However, the respective energy scale is well below the value prescribed by a single-island geometric capacitances. We explain it by strong quantum fluctuations of charge associated with a large value of Josephson energy, $E_J\gg E_C$, where $E_C$ is the charging energy associated with the inter-island capacitance. Comparison between the data and theory points to an exponential (in parameter $E_J/E_C$) suppression of the threshold. We achieve a quantitative agreement with theory by accounting for charge-$e$ solitons associated with the quasiparticles entering the array from its leads. This scenario however underestimates the current below threshold in comparison with the experiment.

titles.title: Coulomb Blockade in a One-Dimensional Array of Strong Josephson Junctions

abstracts.value: Fringes recovered by conditioning on quantum-eraser outcomes do not, by themselves, establish entanglement. We determine the minimum entanglement compatible with recorded eraser data when the preparation may be mixed, distinguishing these data from independently determined optimal which-path distinguishabilities and additional joint measurement outcomes. For noisy Greenberger-Horne-Zeilinger (GHZ) preparations, explicit compatible states establish sharp entanglement-depth thresholds and show how parity information strengthens certification. A matching converse establishes the exact threshold for two complete Pauli-outcome distributions. For an ideal three-qubit eraser, we classify the additional marker measurement directions that certify genuine multipartite entanglement within a fixed eraser configuration and determine the separate minima of compatible concurrence and squared GHZ fidelity for specified tilted axes. For noisy three-qubit data, an exact semidefinite characterization and constructive converse determine biseparable compatibility at arbitrary fixed local measurement axes, with rational certificates bounding one example. These results establish what entanglement is required by the measurement record, rather than inferred from assumptions about the source.

abstracts.value: Charged lepton flavor violation (CLFV) provides a highly sensitive probe of physics beyond the Standard Model. This experimental review discusses $μ^{-} \to e^{-}$ conversion in nuclei, which is a muon CLFV process characterized by a clean monoenergetic-electron signature and the ability to exploit large samples of stopped muons. It describes the physics motivation, basic experimental principles, key background sources, and search strategies, as well as the status and prospects of past and next-generation experiments such as COMET and Mu2e. Future experimental concepts may extend the sensitivity even further. If a signal is observed, comparisons among results obtained with different target nuclei and with those from complementary searches for other muon CLFV decay modes will be essential for identifying the underlying interaction.

titles.title: Experimental Searches for Muon to Electron Conversion in Nuclei

abstracts.value: We calculate the contribution of the $E$-type generalized parton distributions (GPDs) to exclusive dijet electroproduction in $ep\to e'jjp$ in collinear QCD factorization, including both the proton helicity-flipping amplitude and the GPD-$E$ term in the helicity-conserving amplitude, using the double distribution approach for modeling. We include light sea and valence-quark exchanges as well as gluon exchanges and compare the proton helicity-conserving and helicity-flipping contributions for HERA-energy phase space and for Electron-Ion Collider (EIC) kinematics. We find that the helicity-flipping cross section is dominated by valence-quark exchange and has a markedly different dependence on $|t|$ and $x_{\mathbb P}$ from the helicity-conserving contribution. In the EIC kinematics considered here, the helicity-flip contribution becomes comparable to the helicity-conserving one at large $|t|$ and $x_{\mathbb P}$. The results show that exclusive dijet electroproduction can be sensitive to the $E$-type GPDs in the kinematic region accessible at the EIC.

abstracts.value: Measuring BLR size and black hole mass of jetted quasars with strong radio emission is challenging due to the contribution from non-thermal synchrotron radiation from the jet in the optical continuum. Here, we investigate the optical continuum emission in two flat-spectrum radio quasars (FSRQs), PKS~0736+017 and PKS~1510-089, by separating the thermal emission from the accretion disk and the non-thermal synchrotron emission from the jet using their distinct polarization signatures. Our analysis combines multi-epoch optical spectro-photometric and polarimetric observations from the archival optical continuum, H$β$ emission line light curves from earlier reverberation mapping campaigns, and 37 GHz radio data. For PKS~0736+017, we find that the disk contributes approximately 70 % ($f_d = 0.70^{+0.01}_{-0.01}$) of the total optical emission. After removing the jet component, we obtain a revised H$β$ lag of $84.8^{+23.2}_{-18.4}$ days. In contrast, the disk contribution in PKS~1510-089 is lower with 37.5 % ($f_d = 0.37^{+0.01}_{-0.01}$), with a corresponding H$β$ lag of $54.4^{+4.4}_{-5.4}$ days. Our findings highlight the need for careful decomposition of optical light curves in jet-dominated AGN.

titles.title: Decomposition of disk and jet optical emission: Case of PKS~1510-089 and PKS~0736+017

abstracts.value: Circular muon colliders offer a promising route to multi-TeV centre-of-mass energies with high luminosity. The baseline design for the high-energy complex includes a chain of four Rapid-Cycling Synchrotrons (RCSs) accelerating the beam from \qty{63}{\GeV} to \qty5{\TeV}. The chain combines a conventional synchrotron with three hybrid synchrotrons, which use fixed-field superconducting dipoles and rapidly ramped normal-conducting dipoles. The short muon lifetime (\qty{2.2}{\micro\second} in the rest frame) imposes stringent constraints on the acceleration process: achieving the target luminosity requires a muon survival rate of up to \qty{70}{\percent} throughout the acceleration chain, with the full acceleration completed in approximately \qty{10}{\milli\second}. These demanding acceleration conditions raise several beam-dynamics challenges, investigated in this work. First, the impact of the RF cavity distribution on transverse emittance growth is studied. Second, the mismatch between the discretely increasing beam energy and the continuously ramped fields of the pulsed dipoles and quadrupoles is modelled analytically, and its impact is evaluated through tracking simulations. Finally, the sensitivity of the beam trajectory, optical functions, and emittance growth to magnetic-field ramp jitter is assessed.

abstracts.value: Chiral Floquet phases support quantized chiral flow along their boundaries even when the bulk is fully localized. In this Letter, we establish a complementary phenomenon, which we call Hilbert-space pumping: under a boundary condition twisted by time translation, a part of the boundary Hilbert space, of quantized dimension, is transferred between the opposite boundaries. The twist is the temporal analogue of Laughlin's flux insertion in the quantum Hall effect. For noninteracting fermions, the number of transferred boundary modes is determined by the winding number, as we show analytically for the boundary dynamics and numerically for the anomalous Floquet Anderson insulator. For interacting systems whose boundary dynamics is a quantum cellular automaton, the transferred dimension is set by the Gross-Nesme-Vogts-Werner (GNVW) index: the twisted boundary Floquet operator is the Floquet operator on a tilted time slice, whose Hilbert-space dimension is multiplied by the index for each period of twist. We derive this relation for matrix product unitaries and test it numerically in random unitary circuits. Applied to the matrix product operators of non-invertible symmetries, the same twisted rank returns the quantum dimension of the symmetry operator in addition to its flow index.

titles.title: Quantized pumping of boundary Hilbert space in chiral Floquet phases

abstracts.value: Estimating several phases simultaneously is more than estimating them one at a time: the optimal measurements for different parameters may not commute, and in a multiparameter problem the quantum Cramér-Rao bound is not automatically achievable. Ring cavities are a natural setting for this question, since a single coherent input can be made to interact repeatedly with every internal phase before it is read out. We study the simultaneous local estimation of the $n$ internal phases of a lossless $n$-port ring cavity probed by a fixed-energy multimode coherent state, optimizing over the full coherent-input space and over the operating point of the cavity. We identify a necessary and sufficient condition for the global optimum: the input energy should be distributed equally among the ports, and the internal phases and input phases satisfy a simple phase-matching condition for every port. The optimum is unique up to a common optical phase and minimizes both the symmetric logarithmic derivative (SLD) cost and the sloppiness of the model. At this point the quantum Fisher information matrix is full rank and its spectrum is obtained in closed form, the Uhlmann curvature vanishes, and no incompatibility penalty has to be paid. The precision retains the coherent-state scaling and the dependence on the number of phases, but the cavity feedback reduces the prefactor relative to $n$ independent single-pass experiments. Finally, we show that this bound may be achieved in practice: the Fisher information of a balanced homodyne measurement at each output port, with local-oscillator phases locked to the prepared input phases is equal to the optimal quantum Fisher information. Our results establish the ring cavity as a platform for optimal multiphase sensing and provide the ultimate benchmark against which nonclassical probes may be evaluated for further precision enhancement.

titles.title: Single-port homodyne detection achieves optimal multiphase sensing in an $n$-port ring cavity

abstracts.value: Superinsulation is the confining phase of condensed matter systems. It is a genuine quantum state of matter, dual to superconductivity, just as confinement in particle physics is dual to the Higgs phase. In contrast to hadron physics, the gauge field that becomes confining is not colour SU(3) but the conventional U(1) electromagnetic field. Superinsulation arises in superconductors with an emergent granular condensate when core-less XY vortices between condensate grains become tensionless, unobservable Dirac strings and magnetic monopoles are liberated and condense. This magnetic condensate confines electric fields into flux tubes, strings that generate a linear potential between Cooper pairs. These dual Abrikosov flux tubes give rise to infinite electrical resistance, persisting up to a finite deconfinement temperature. We shall review the theoretical framework of superinsulation together with its experimental validation, including the direct observation of the linear confining potential and we shall stress how phase-only approaches and disorder-based ideas for the phases around the superconductor-to-insulator transition are hard to reconcile with recent experimental observations.

titles.title: Superinsulation, electric confinement in condensed matter

abstracts.value: The interaction between relativistic electron beams and plasma can generate magnetic fields with strengths of $\sim 10^4$ T far exceeding conventional magnets, which offers a promising environment for producing weakly coupled particles. Using particle-in-cell simulations incorporating an axion-emission model, we show that a 10-GeV electron beam traversing dense plasma emits a forward-collimated axion beam during the ion-mediated nonlinear stage of current filamentation instability. Although the electron-driven linear instability seeds the filaments, ion motion governs their subsequent expansion and coalescence. This evolution reinjects cold-core electrons into large-amplitude orbits in phase space, where they repeatedly cross the strong-field flanks of neighboring magnetic vortices, thereby enhancing axion emission. At a background-plasma density of $\sim 10^{21}\mathrm{cm}^{-3}$, suppressing ion motion reduces the axion yield by a factor of 14.5. Our results demonstrate that ion dynamics play a crucial role in characterizing the emission of weakly coupled particles induced by relativistic filamentation instabilities, suggesting a new beam-driven method for probing the axion-electron interaction at accelerators.

abstracts.value: Unitary synthesis complexity studies the computational cost of applying a target unitary to an unknown quantum state, extending complexity theory beyond its traditional focus on problems with classical inputs and outputs. Rosenthal and Yuen (ITCS 2022) introduced two complexity classes for unitary synthesis: $\mathsf{unitaryQIP}$ and $\mathsf{unitaryPSPACE}$ for the unitary families implementable via interactive proofs and in polynomial space, respectively. In this work, we prove the equality $\mathsf{unitaryQIP}=\mathsf{unitaryPSPACE}$ and thereby establish a unitary-complexity analogue of $\mathsf{QIP} = \mathsf{PSPACE}$ (Jain, Ji, Upadhyay, and Watrous, J. ACM 2011) and $\mathsf{stateQIP}=\mathsf{statePSPACE}$ (Rosenthal and Yuen, ITCS 2022; Metger and Yuen, FOCS 2023). To prove $\mathsf{unitaryQIP} \subseteq \mathsf{unitaryPSPACE}$, we use an acceptance rigidity lemma derived from the soundness condition to show that the polynomial-space prover constructed for a fixed input in state synthesis (Metger and Yuen, FOCS 2023) implements the target unitary on every input, leading to a polynomial-space simulation of the protocol. For the reverse inclusion, we build on OpenAI's recently announced solution to the unitary synthesis problem (Aaronson and Kuperberg, Theory Comput. 2007), and show that $\mathsf{unitaryPSPACE}$ families can be synthesized in polynomial time with a $\mathsf{PSPACE}$ oracle. We then implement the oracle queries using auxiliary states prepared via the $\mathsf{statePSPACE} \subseteq \mathsf{stateQIP}$ protocol (Rosenthal and Yuen, ITCS 2022). Beyond the equality, we show that our protocol for $\mathsf{unitaryPSPACE}$ can be parallelized to constant rounds when the verifier receives polynomially many copies of the input, and we also obtain a complexity-theoretic barrier to proving the existence of $\mathsf{EFI}$ pairs.

titles.title: unitaryQIP = unitaryPSPACE

abstracts.value: We experimentally demonstrate the generation of needle-like beams from spontaneous parametric downconversion (SPDC) light using a compact inverse-designed multilevel diffractive lens (MDL). The nonclassical nature of the SPDC source is independently verified through a three-detector heralded Hanbury Brown-Twiss measurement performed before the MDL, yielding a zero-delay second-order correlation value of approximately 0.14. Spatial measurements using an intensified charge-coupled device reveal that the MDL maintains a tightly confined focal distribution over an axial distance of approximately 11 mm under collinear SPDC illumination, substantially reducing diffraction-induced broadening compared with a conventional plano-convex lens of the same nominal focal length. Under non-collinear SPDC illumination, two distinct regions of extended axial confinement are observed, demonstrating the dependence of the engineered focal distribution on the incident spatial field. These results establish a compact flat-optical approach for engineering extended-focus SPDC photon fields, with potential applications in structured quantum photonics.

titles.title: Needle-beam generation from SPDC photons using inverse-designed flat optics

abstracts.value: We present an X-ray study of the high-synchrotron-peaked blazar Mrk 421 using ten days of XPoSat/XSPECT observations (2025 January 20-29; 202 ks) and contemporaneous NICER data. The 0.8-15 keV light curve has a fractional variability amplitude of 19.6 +/- 0.3 per cent, and Bayesian blocks resolve 26 flux states spanning a factor of 2.3. The best-constrained flare has a fast rise and a slow decay, with e-folding times of about 3 h and 30 h. For typical jet parameters, the X-ray-emitting electrons cool faster than this, suggesting that the decay traces a gradual weakening of their acceleration. The count-rate distribution is best described by two lognormal components, consistent with multiplicative variability. The power spectrum is a red-noise power law with a slope of about 1.7 over timescales of 25 min to 10 d, typical of blazars. XSPECT and NICER count rates are well correlated over eight matched epochs (r = 0.941). We fitted log-parabola models to day-resolved spectra from XSPECT, NICER and both jointly, and to flux-resolved XSPECT spectra. Both show spectral hardening with brightness. In the flux-resolved spectra, the photon index at 1 keV decreases from 2.24 in the faintest state to 1.96 in the brightest, and the synchrotron peak moves from about 0.66 to 1.06 keV, while the curvature ($β\approx 0.7$) shows no significant change. Power-law fits to Bayesian blocks show that bright blocks at the same rate can differ in photon index by up to $6.4σ$, so count rate alone does not fix the spectral state.

titles.title: X-ray Variability of Mrk 421 in 2025 January: A Ten-Day XPoSat XSPECT Campaign with Contemporaneous NICER Coverage

abstracts.value: A seven dimensional theory with branes, described by a Transgression Action is investigated. The theory has special properties owing to the factorization of the trace used to define the Transgression form. It is shown that in some cases the theory is similar to the models of branes proposed by Nepomechie, Wu and Zee as a higher dimensional generalization of models of particles with fractional statistics of Wilczek, Wu and Zee. Static Euclidean solutions are presented, and compared with similar solutions of Nepomechie,Wu and Zee. Then Lorentzian static solutions are considered, based in solutions of constant curvature black holes presented by Bañados and further studied by Guilleminot, Olea and Petrov. Topological phases and their implications for quantum statistics are discussed.

abstracts.value: Electron--positron pair production in spatially and temporally inhomogeneous electric fields is investigated in $1+1$ dimensions within the Dirac--Heisenberg--Wigner (DHW) formalism. We consider a composite field formed by two Gaussian pulses with independently adjustable spatial widths, $λ_1$ and $λ_2$, extending commonly used combined-pulse configurations in which the constituent pulses share the same spatial envelope. Both temporally overlapping and temporally separated configurations are analyzed. For overlapping pulses, decreasing $λ_2$ at fixed $λ_1$ enlarges the weak-field region and enhances the low-momentum part of the particle spectrum. Oscillatory temporal profiles further increase the particle yield while reducing the net momentum transferred to the particles. For temporally separated pulses, the spatial width of the delayed pulse determines the extent to which it accelerates particles created by the earlier pulse. A narrow delayed pulse affects only a limited fraction of these particles, whereas a broader pulse substantially reshapes the final momentum distribution. These results identify the spatial-width disparity between the constituent pulses as an additional control parameter for Schwinger pair production in multicomponent electric fields.

titles.title: Schwinger Pair Production in Superposed Electric-Field Pulses with Distinct Spatial Widths

abstracts.value: The response of the Jaynes--Cummings (JC) model to strong driving has been examined previously, but the origin of intriguing features near emitter--cavity resonance remains poorly understood because of the large background in conventional transmission spectroscopy. Here we introduce a spectroscopic approach for circuit quantum electrodynamics that combines strong cavity driving with quantum-nondemolition qubit readout. Separating the drive and readout substantially enhances the measurement sensitivity as compared with conventional cavity-transmission spectroscopy. With this technique, we identify the near-resonant features as multiphoton transitions between emitter--photon dressed states of the same parity, and resolve transitions between dressed states of opposite parity. Away from resonance, we also observe selective enhancement and suppression of multiphoton transitions, together with transitions involving the second excited state of the anharmonic qubit. Our approach opens a route to resolving the rich transition structure of the JC ladder and probing strongly driven light--matter interactions.

titles.title: Quantum-Nondemolition Probing of Multiphoton Transitions between Dressed States in a Strongly Driven Jaynes--Cummings System

abstracts.value: The next generation of Stage-V spectroscopic surveys are designed to measure hundreds of millions of galaxy and quasar spectra, extending precision large-scale-structure cosmology to redshifts and volumes well beyond the reach of current Stage-IV facilities. Realising this potential requires revisiting the target selection strategies and designing them explicitly around the depth, multiplexing, and survey time of the new instruments, rather than a direct extrapolation of existing recipes. This work develops and characterises new strategies for the Wide-field Spectroscopic Telescope (WST), a proposed 12-metre, highly multiplexed facility expected to operate in the 2040s. Using deep multi-band photometry, including COSMOS-field data from CLAUDS and HSC, we revisit low-redshift $z<1.6$ tracer selection of SDSS, BOSS/eBOSS, DESI and 4MOST-CRS -- Bright Galaxies, Luminous Red Galaxies, Emission Line Galaxies and quasars -- to photometric depth achievable in the WST era, and introduce a purely magnitude-limited sample (MagMax) exploiting three-dimensional colour-colour star-galaxy separation, and a set of Lyman-Break Galaxy dropout samples extending target selection to $z>2$. Using Fisher-matrix forecasts, we showcase the constraining power of a WST-like cosmological survey on BAO distance parameters $α_\parallel$ and $α_\perp$, the growth rate $f$, the evolving dark energy equation $w_0w_a$, the local-type primordial non-Gaussianity $f_{\rm NL}^{\rm loc}$, and the sum of the neutrino mass $Σm_ν$. The main outcome of this work is an optimisation framework that directly links instrumental capabilities and observing time to cosmological constraining power, providing a science-driven template applicable to the design of future generations of Stage-V spectroscopic surveys.

titles.title: Targeting the future of spectroscopic galaxy surveys -- A cosmological study case with the Wide-field Spectroscopic Telescope

abstracts.value: No consensus has been reached on the appropriate operators for the spin and orbital angular momentum of free relativistic electrons. But there is a tendency to believe the existence of a spin-orbit coupling through the Berry connection. Here we show that this is not the case. Because the positive-energy solution of the Dirac equation is associated with the state of the electron, it is reasonable to postulate that only when projected onto the positive-energy subspace can observable operators on the Hilbert space of the Dirac equation represent physical quantities of the electron. On this basis, we find, after mapping the projected operators onto an irreducible representation, that the Berry connection describes the position of a quantum reference point with respect to the laboratory reference frame, relative to which the position of the electron is canonical. The orbital angular momentum of the quantum reference point about the origin of the laboratory reference frame is expressed in terms of the Berry connection. It combines with the canonical orbital angular momentum of the electron about the quantum reference point to give the orbital angular momentum of the electron about the origin of the laboratory reference frame.

titles.title: On physical origin of Berry connection of free relativistic electrons

abstracts.value: One of the major challenges of implementing high-rate quantum error correction codes, like qLDPC codes, is realizing the required long-range interactions. Spin qubit platforms can provide this connectivity by shuttling qubits next to each other whenever they need to interact. When doing this, the performance of the code depends on the shuttling strategy. We study memory experiments of the [[144,12,12]] bivariate bicycle (Gross) code on two shuttling grids for future spin qubit devices: a square grid and a square grid with diagonals. We compare three shuttling strategies, structured and random initial layouts, and a range of shuttling noise models spanning best- and worst-case scenarios. The best strategy minimizes the longest distance travelled rather than the total distance. The initial layout has only a weak effect, whereas adding diagonals to the grid reduces the logical error rate by up to two orders of magnitude which may have implications for future hardware design.

titles.title: Towards Optimal Routing Strategies for qLDPC codes on Silicon Spin Qubits

abstracts.value: Global polarization of $Λ$, $Ξ$, and $Ω$ hyperons is measured in Au+Au collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\mathrm{NN}}}=7.7$, 9.2, 11.5, 14.6, 17.3, 19.6, and 27~GeV using high-statistics data from the second phase of the RHIC Beam Energy Scan. No significant difference between the $Λ$ and $\barΛ$ polarizations is observed over the measured collision-energy range, providing improved constraints on magnetic-field-induced contributions. The $Λ$ polarization increases with the magnitude of rapidity, with the slope of the linear fit differing from zero by 4.8 standard deviations, providing the first evidence for a nonzero rapidity dependence of global polarization in this energy range. Global polarization of $Ξ^{-}+\barΞ^{+}$ is observed for the first time at these energies at a significance exceeding 5 standard deviations, with a magnitude comparable to that of $Λ+\barΛ$ and an increase toward lower collision energies. Measurements of $Ω^{-}+\barΩ^{+}$ are compatible with a similar energy dependence and favor the decay parameter $γ_Ω= +1$ with high probability under the assumption of the global polarization picture. These measurements provide new constraints on the energy evolution, rapidity dependence, and species dependence of global polarization in heavy-ion collisions.

abstracts.value: Driving a many-particle quantum system with an appropriately tuned external field can give rise to features in its nonequilibrium dynamics that are absent in the equilibrium counterpart. Cooperative dynamics in a dense ensemble of quantum emitters manifested through superradiance, a burst in the emission intensity as a function of time, is typically suppressed by spectral disparities among emitters in the ensemble. We demonstrate the enhancement of cooperative dynamics in a spectrally inhomogeneous ensemble of quantum emitters when it is driven by a periodic pulse sequence. Using both a semi-analytical mean-field solution and a digital quantum simulation, we examine the coherence of the pulse-driven ensemble and the intensity of the emitted radiation as a function of the spectral disparity in the ensemble, as a function of time, the number of atoms in the system, and as a function of the inter-pulse delay. We identify clear signatures of the enhanced cooperative dynamics for the pulse-driven inhomogeneous ensemble when dephasing in the dynamics of the ensemble is suppressed by a sufficient number of pulses during the individual emitter lifetime. These results demonstrate a post-fabrication tuning knob based on externally applied control fields for the dynamics of the many-emitter ensemble.

titles.title: Inducing cooperative dynamics in an inhomogeneous many-emitter ensemble with a pulse sequence

abstracts.value: Quantum software ecosystems provide increasingly capable tools for simulation and hardware execution, but differences in programming models, supported features, and backend capabilities can make it difficult to move and systematically compare the same quantum algorithm across execution environments. We introduce eigenkit, a provider-neutral quantum computing library that separates algorithm definition from backend execution through a common circuit representation and provider interface. The library currently supports 12 execution providers spanning simulators and quantum hardware, provides backend-independent gradient computation, and integrates with standard scientific-computing and machine-learning workflows through NumPy, PyTorch, and scikit-learn interfaces. We evaluate the practical relevance of this abstraction across both simulation and quantum hardware. Simulator performance varies substantially with circuit size, structure, batching, and application workload, showing that no single backend is consistently preferable. On quantum hardware, experiments on IBM Heron and IQM Emerald show that which processor is better suited to a given algorithm depends not only on hardware constraints, but also on how well the topology of the quantum algorithm matches the physical connectivity of the processor. These results demonstrate that backend portability is not only a software-design convenience, but can be important for both computational efficiency and quantum execution quality.

titles.title: eigenkit: A Provider-Neutral Quantum Computing Library

abstracts.value: Directionally generating and controlling quantum states is critical in chiral quantum technologies. Here, we propose a scheme for the nonreciprocal generation of Bell states via cooperative dissipation in a qubit-magnon system, consisting of a superconducting transmon qubit and a yttrium iron garnet sphere subject to a bias magnetic field. The cooperative dissipation between them is induced by coupling both to a common transmission-line waveguide. Due to this cooperative dissipation, the system possesses a dark eigenstate within the single-excitation subspace. Under appropriate parameter conditions, the dark eigenstate reduces to a specific Bell state. With the assistance of a drive pulse, the system can be prepared in this Bell state (i.e., the dark eigenstate). In particular, we find that the dark eigenstate corresponds to different Bell states under positive ($+\mathbf{B}_0$) and negative ($-\mathbf{B}_0$) bias fields. Consequently, nonreciprocal Bell-state generation is achieved: $+\mathbf{B}_0$ yields one Bell state, while $-\mathbf{B}_0$ yields the other. Moreover, we define a fidelity-based nonreciprocal rate to quantify this nonreciprocity. Our work establishes cooperative dissipation as a versatile resource for nonreciprocal entangled-state generation, opening a promising route toward chiral quantum technologies.

titles.title: Nonreciprocal generation of Bell states via cooperative dissipation in a qubit-magnon system

abstracts.value: Thermodynamics typically assumes that a system in contact with a thermal reservoir relaxes to the Gibbs state, or to the grand canonical Gibbs state when it also exchanges particles. However, this only holds when the coupling is very weak. Beyond this, the expected equilibrium state is the mean force Gibbs (MFG) state, obtained by tracing the reservoir out of the thermal state of the combined system. Despite its relevance, general analytic results for the MFG state have so far been obtained almost exclusively for bosonic reservoirs. Here we derive the grand canonical MFG state to second order in the coupling for a generic fermionic system coupled to a thermal reservoir at arbitrary chemical potential, using the concept of the mode reduced state in order for the fermionic MFG state to be well defined. The correction to the bare Gibbs state separates into particle and hole channels weighted by the empty and occupied reservoir states, related through the Kubo-Martin-Schwinger condition. We apply the result to the resonant level model, two modes coupled to a shared reservoir, and the single impurity Anderson model. For the two modes, the reservoir mediates coherence between modes that do not interact directly, something the bare Gibbs state cannot capture. We verify our results against numerically exact calculations, including real-time dynamics for the interacting model, and find agreement between the static prediction and the dynamical relaxation.

titles.title: Second-order mean force Gibbs state of fermionic open systems

abstracts.value: In this work, we show that the $X(3790)$ reported by the BESIII Collaboration is unlikely to be a genuine resonance, a conclusion that follows from the incompleteness of the BESIII experimental analysis. Although BESIII included the established charmed mesons that couple to $Dπ$, as listed by the Particle Data Group, and incorporated their reflections in the $D^0D^-$ invariant mass spectrum, this fit to the experimental data does not exhaust the charmed mesons that can contribute to the $D^0D^-$ invariant mass spectrum through reflections, as can be explicitly seen from a theoretical charmed-meson spectroscopy. We find that a predicted charmed meson, either $D(3\,{}^3S_1)$ or $D(2\,{}^3D_1)$, can play a crucial role in mimicking the $X(3790)$ structure through the corresponding reflection. This warrants caution in interpreting the $X(3790)$ as a genuine resonance. Moreover, such an interpretation is not supported by most theoretical studies of $D\bar{D}$ hadronic molecules and compact $c\bar{c}d\bar{u}$ tetraquarks currently available.
